publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper will provide an overview of the major recent activities of the CCEM inculding matters related to the fundamental constants and the SI like the work on electrical methods to monitor the stability of the kilogram and the status of the leastsquares adjustment of the fundamental constants. Of particular interest to the CCEM is the work involving improvements in the knowledge of KJ and RK, the Josephson and von Klitzing constants.

articleTitle: Femtosecond optical clock
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Summary form only given. Results on creation of new generation compact optical clock using highly stable femtosecond light pulses are presented. Femtosecond optical synthesizers allowing absolute frequency measurements from the optical to the radio range with an accuracy of 10/sup -16/ and higher are considered. New results of optical frequency measurements at transitions of atoms and molecules are reported.

articleTitle: NIST 0.05-50 GHz direct comparison power calibration system
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper describes the development of a 2.4 mm power calibration service at NIST. The service operates over a frequency range of 0.05 to 50 GHz. The primary focus of the paper is a direct-comparison system for calibrating thermistor, thin-film, and thermoelectric power detectors.

articleTitle: A micromechanical DC-voltage reference
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Prototype of a novel DC voltage reference has been constructed. A characteristic voltage of an electrostatically actuated micromechanical silicon device provides the reference voltage. Its stability relies on elastic properties of monocrystalline silicon. The device is suited for batch fabrication and may prove more stable than Zener voltage references.

articleTitle: A new method for measuring ratios of dc voltages from 10 V to 1100 V
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new reference-step method is described for measuring the ratio of two dc voltages in the range, 10 V to 1100 V, not covered by the Josephson voltage standard. The method requires a voltmeter and switchable voltage source and can achieve uncertainties of a few parts in 10/sup 7/ of the ratio.

articleTitle: A cryogenic current comparator resistance ratio bridge for the range 10 k/spl Omega/ to 1 G/spl Omega/
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A cryogenic current comparator with a potential current noise of 1 fA//spl radic/Hz has been built. The comparator will provide accurate current ratios for a new high resistance bridge, using a novel method of balancing two currents from a single source.

articleTitle: New ac-dc transfer step-up calibration and uncertainty calculation in PTB and INTI
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: In PTB and INTI new ac-dc voltage transfer standards are built for the voltage range of 0.1 V to 1000 V and the frequency range of 10 Hz to 1 MHz. PMJTC (Planar Multijunction Thermal Converters) and coaxial voltage dropping resistors are used in the step-up procedure for the different voltage levels. For voltages >100 V new planar resistors are used to guarantee voltage independence of the ac-dc transfer difference. The high sensitivity of the PMJTC allows big steps in the step-up calibration and many steps inbetween which leads to an overdetermined system to check the validity of the assumptions used in the step-up. The uncertainty budget for the different voltage levels is calculated.

articleTitle: Design analysis of a sapphire loaded cavity for a spaceborne hydrogen maser
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: TE/sub 011/ mode of a sapphire cavity for H-maser was analytically solved, and the quality factor and filling factor was calculated as well as oscillation power and stability. Based on the analysis, a sapphire cavity was developed and its measured characteristics agreed very well with the analysis.

articleTitle: Complex compactly-supported orthonormal wavelets: constructions and applications in power system
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Summary form only given. The essence of the wavelet transform (WT) is to measure the local similarity between two waveforms: a signal and a wavelet. The waveform of a signal or a wavelet depends not only on its magnitude spectrum (MSP) but also on its phase spectrum (PSP). How well the PSP of a wavelet matches the PSP of a signal greatly influences the WT efficiency. On the other hand, phase information which can be extracted by a complex WT is important in power systems. The ability to extract phase information is crucial for a wavelet to be used in power systems. Compactly-supported (in time-domain) orthonormal wavelets (CSOWs) have an excellent property in that their analysis and synthesis filters are the same, and are finite impulse response type. WTs and inverse WTs with CSOWs can be implemented easily and quickly. However, all the existing CSOWs are real ones. It is impossible to extract phase information of a signal under analysis by them. Another drawback of CSOWs is their poor PSPs. This makes them behave not very well when the signals have a variety of PSPs. This paper describes how to construct a large number of complex CSOWs with various PSPs from existing real CSOWs, and how to take combined information (CI) from a complex WT instead of the more usually used simple information (SI), in order to highlight slight distinctions between similar signals in more detail. A number of simulated applications in power systems demonstrate that the derived complex wavelets are more superior to the original ones and so is CI to SI.

articleTitle: Calibration of multimeters as voltage ratio standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report on measurements for the evaluation of the linearity of DVMs in use in our laboratories, aimed at determining the performances in the /spl plusmn/V range of commercial multimeters as voltage ratio standard. The evaluation of deviations from linearity in the selected range becomes important in measurements of resistance ratios, where voltage limitations may exist. After calibration, uncertainty below 0.1 ppm can be obtained.

articleTitle: Voltage divider characterisation at frequencies up to 200 kHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The paper describes new techniques of measuring angular and in-phase errors of voltage dividers at frequencies up to 200 kHz. Preliminary investigations indicate uncertainties of 400 /spl mu/rad and 50 /spl mu/V/V at voltages up to 240 V and frequencies up to 200 kHz.

articleTitle: Cryogenic sapphire oscillator with exceptionally high frequency stability
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Extremely high short-term frequency stability has been realised in oscillators based on liquid helium cooled sapphire resonators with a modified mounting structure. These oscillators have exhibited an Allan deviation of about 5.4/spl times/10/sup -16//spl tau//sup -1/2/ for integration times (/spl tau/) of 1 to 4 s and a minimum of 2.4/spl times/10/sup -16/ at 32 s.

articleTitle: Comparison of capacitance with resistance by IVD-based quadrature bridge at frequencies from 50 Hz to 10 kHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A quadrature bridge capable of comparing capacitance with resistance at frequencies from 50 Hz to 10 kHz is described. To balance the bridge at a wide frequency range, three two-stage inductive voltage dividers (IVD) are used. By using this bridge, we can precisely decide capacitance standards at 50 Hz, 60 Hz, 400 Hz and 1 kHz, which are frequently demanded by industry.

articleTitle: Evaluation of AC-DC transfer standards in the mV-range
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Four different methods used to establish traceability of AC-voltage in the mV-range are discussed. From a reference level based on multijunction thermal converters, voltage step-down is made using thermal voltage converters, micropotentiometers and resistive voltage dividers. A method based on summing of AC-voltages is also used. The results of the different methods are compared and found to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: The dual mixer time difference at IEN
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report the results obtained with a frequency instability measurement system based upon the dual-mixer time-difference scheme working at 10 MHz with a 1 Hz beat note. It shows a two samples (Allan deviation) measurement floor of 5.6.10/sup -14///spl tau/ and a temperature sensitivity of some picoseconds per Celsius.

articleTitle: A broadband microwave total power radiometer
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A temperature stabilized and null-balanced broadband microwave radiometer of the total power type has been designed and its usefulness experimentally tested and evaluated at X-band.

articleTitle: A simple traceable current transformer calibration method
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A simple traceable mains-frequency current transformer ratio build-up scheme has been developed which enables calibration of ratios from 5 A:5 A to 500 A:5 A with uncertainties of 0.05 /spl mu/A/A and 0.05 /spl mu/rad. The build-up is based on series-parallel interchange of primary windings of two-stage transformers with magnetically shielded second stages.

articleTitle: The numerical calculation of magnetic shielding effectiveness of comparator based on FEM
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new numerical method used to calculate the magnetic shielding effectiveness of comparator is given in this paper. This method has been applied in the heavy current comparator we designed, the result is quite ideal.

articleTitle: Influence of time delay in calibration systems for instrument transformers with digital output
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Calibration of instrument transformers with digital output requires determination of the time delay in the digital system. The time delay of reference systems must therefore be accurately known. Measurements on SP's measurement system have shown the time delay to be 190/spl plusmn/21 ns. This result is very promising and adequate for the system.

articleTitle: Automated DC voltage divider to calibrate voltages up to 1 kV
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A voltage divider has been developed to calibrate DC voltages up to 1 kV. The ratio of the divider can be automatically self-calibrated. The expected uncertainty is several parts per 10/sup 8/ for the self-calibration of voltage ratio of 1 kV to 1 V.

articleTitle: Inductive voltage dividers comparison with a vector voltmeter
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A setup for calibration of inductive voltage dividers, based on a vector voltmeter with very high common-mode-rejection-ratio (CMRR), is described. The voltmeter is built with a differential amplifier and a lock-in board, both enclosed in a guard, completely battery-operated and interfaced with optical fiber links. An implementation with commercial instrumentation is tested and first results are shown.

articleTitle: Reproduction of the loss angle unit of VNIIM
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The primary standard of the loss angle unit containing special capacitors and a transformer bridge, has been developed at VNIIM. Different methods for reproduction of the unit are used, the measurement results agree within 0.1 /spl mu/rad at the frequency 1 kHz. The measurement uncertainty is /spl plusmn/0.2 /spl mu/rad, k=2.

articleTitle: The national inductance standard in NIM
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A modified Maxwell bridge has been made from several sets of Wilkins resistors and two boxes combined with a capacitor and a conductance with a IVD. The paper proposes a method that can eliminate the effect of the resistance time constant and emphasizes how to design a source balance network.

articleTitle: Improvements in the NIST cryogenic thermal transfer standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Recent improvements in the prototype of an ac-dc thermal transfer standard operating at cryogenic temperatures are described. Descriptions of two new transmission lines are presented, along with ac-dc difference measurements and Fast-Reversed DC (FRDC) data. Future plans for this project are also discussed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of capacitance and resistance standards at higher frequencies
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Four terminal-pair (4TP) capacitance and resistance standards were compared against coaxial standards up to 15 MHz using a four terminal pair impedance analyzer. Both commercial and custom designed 4TP to coaxial adapters were used and evaluated in the measurement process. Coaxial standards were measured on RF reflection coefficient measuring system. Measurement results were compared to those obtained by other techniques and circuit modeling predictions. The agreement within 0.1% at 10 MHz for the capacitance or resistance part of admittance was sought.

articleTitle: An optically modulated field sensor to make TEM cells traceable to the NPL calculable standard dipole antenna
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper describes the evaluation of an electric field sensor based on a lithium niobate optical modulator, and also the modifications made to the field sensor system to improve its performance. The results of the calibration of the sensor against the NPL calculable standard dipole antenna, and also in three transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cells are presented. These indicate that the antenna factor of the modified field sensor system is stable to within /spl plusmn/0.3 dB. Further development of the system is outlined.

articleTitle: QHE array resistance standards down to 129 /spl Omega/
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper deals with the development and the study of novel QHE resistance standards of expected values as low as R/sub K//200. We report first results of measurement obtained on devices made of 100 Hall bars placed in parallel by triple connections. The good agreement of the Hall resistance with the nominal value at a level of one part in 10/sup 8/ proves the high potential of these structures as future standards for material resistor calibration, international comparisons and self bridge calibrations.

articleTitle: Uncertainty analysis of a DVM-based quantum Hall measurement set-up
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A detailed uncertainty analysis is presented of a quantum Hall measurement set-up based on a digital voltmeter (DVM) that has been developed at the NMi Van Swinden Laboratorium. Special attention is paid to the uncertainty contributions that arise from the DVMs being used.

articleTitle: Estimation of errors of voltage transformers on-site and the uncertainty of the estimate
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A deregulated energy market needs demonstrably correct energy measurements for correct billing. Voltage transformers may be prone to drift implying a need for verification of their errors. A method to do this on-site using previous calibrations and comparative measurements has been developed and its uncertainty has been estimated.

articleTitle: 1 volt Josephson fast reversed dc source
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have made several improvements to the NIST Josephson FRDC (fast reversed dc) source so that it now operates at 1 volt. We have made a precision comparison to a conventional semiconductor FRDC source by measuring the thermoelectric transfer difference of known thermal voltage converts. The agreement between the two sources was measured to be better than 1 part in 10/sup 7/.

articleTitle: Improved modelling of the coaxial Kelvin balance
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We present the results of a model of the Kelvin balance commonly used in four-terminal coaxial bridges. A Kelvin balance is used to combine the low-potential terminals of two impedances into a single potential. The model considers the effect of interconnecting cables, equalisers, and shunt impedances within the measured impedances.

articleTitle: AC quantised Hall resistance measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We are currently undertaking a project to compare the quantised Hall resistance at AC with the primary capacitance standard, the calculable cross-capacitor, at a range of frequencies (200 Hz-2 kHz). We report on planned measurements and progress to date.

articleTitle: Comparison of two cesium fountain primary frequency standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Two cesium fountain frequency standards are now in operation at BNM-LPTF, FO1 and the transportable PHARAO fountain. We present a first accuracy evaluation of the PHARAO fountain, a new evaluation of FO1, and a frequency comparison between both clocks. They are found to agree to better than 2/spl times/10/sup -15/.

articleTitle: Traceable antenna-gain measurement in a single-antenna setup
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A method is (re)introduced to measure the gain factor of a single passive antenna. A setup for insertion loss measurement and the antenna itself in front of a totally reflecting surface is required simulating a second identical antenna speeding up calibrations considerably with traceable results, smaller uncertainty and cost.

articleTitle: High value resistance standards at ETL
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: High value resistance standards has been established at ETL. Precision programmable voltage sources are used as ratio arm of bridge. Resistive network has been made in order to calibrate the ratio of output voltage of programmable voltage sources.

articleTitle: High resistance measurement at NIM
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An automatic ratio bridge based on BVD is used to take measurement up to 1 G/spl Omega/ at NIM. Adopting a "Virtual Null" mode efficiently reduces effects of insulation of bridge and offset current of detector. The measurement of a 100 M/spl Omega/ Hamon resistor shows an agreement of 1 parts in 10/sup 6/ at ratio 1 G/spl Omega/:100 M/spl Omega/.

articleTitle: A quantum Hall cryogenic current comparator resistance bridge
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A cryogenic current comparator (CCC) bridge for measuring quantum Hall resistance standards is described. The necessity for a full build-up calibration of the CCC is demonstrated and a model of the servo system for controlling the bridge is given.

articleTitle: Development and evaluation of a high resolution measuring system for a switching impulse measurement
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper describes development and evaluation of a high accuracy high voltage measuring system for switching impulse. The noise level is less than 0.05%, the estimated uncertainties for the peak value measurement are better than +0.1%; for the time parameter measurement better than +1%.

articleTitle: A micromechanical RMS-to-DC converter
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A micromechanical silicon device has been designed for use as a precise batch-fabricated AC voltage to DC voltage converter. The converter measures the difference of the electrostatic RMS forces induced by AC and DC voltages.

articleTitle: Noise-source stability measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report results of stability tests on several noise sources for selected frequencies between 12 and 26.5 GHz. Measurements covered intervals of about 1 week and about 1 year or more. Drifts in noise temperature were typically less than the uncertainty of the tests, about 0.03% per day or about 0.05% per year for hot sources.

articleTitle: Improvements in the PSB AC-DC transfer capabilities and a proposal for range extension
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new automated AC-DC transfer calibration system based on thin-film multijunction thermal converter as primary standards at low-frequency range 10 Hz to 1 MHz has been designed and developed. Range extension up to 1000 V is achieved using resistive voltage divider. An equally-divided range extension setup which can be self-calibrated under practical working conditions has been proposed and eliminate the need of voltage interpolation.

articleTitle: Six-port based wave-correlator
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A novel method for calibrating six-port based wave-correlators is reported in this paper. The calibration procedure uses only one phase shifter and offers simple formulas for determining the calibration parameters. Some experiments using a new six-port junction for the wave-correlator at X-band frequency was carried out and the results confirmed the validity and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Diode-laser-based light sources for laser cooling of trapped Yb/sup +/ ions
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We are developing a light source at 370 nm for driving the /sup 2/S/sub 1/2/-/sup 2/P/sub 1/2/ cooling transition by sum-frequency mixing of radiation from two diode lasers with a doubly resonant external cavity. To drive the /sup 2/D/sub 3/2/-/sup 3/D[3/2]/sub 1/2/ repumping transition at 935 nm, we developed two types of external cavity diode lasers. Applications of them to laser-cooled trapped Yb/sup +/ ions are also presented.

articleTitle: ETL open-area site for antenna measurement
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An open-area antenna site for measurement of standard antennas was built in the second research center of the Agency of Industrial Science and Technology. It has a ground plane whose dimension is 50 m long by 30 m wide. The outline of the facility is described.

articleTitle: A new fabrication process for planar thin-film multijunction thermal converters
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Advanced thin film processing and packaging technologies are employed in the fabrication of new planar thin-film multijunction thermal converters. The processing, packaging, and design features build on experience gained from prior NIST demonstrations of thin-film converters with optimizations for improved sensitivity, bandwidth, manufacturability, and reliability.

articleTitle: Measurements of near-field shielding effectiveness by small loop antennas
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: On the basis of the theoretical analysis, we evaluated the magnetic field and the near-field shielding effectiveness of a metallic shielding plate by measurements. His shown the near-field shielding effectiveness is different depending on the orientation of a transmitting and probe loop antennas and on the sizes of the shielding plates.

articleTitle: Methane optical frequency standard on recoil doublet components
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The He-Ne/CH/sub 4/ laser frequency standard using recoil doublet components as a reference was under investigation. The frequency shifts for different parameters were measured. These experiments allow us to estimate the reproducibility of the methane standard of 10/sup -14/.

articleTitle: Thermal cesium beam frequency standard with optical pumping at CENAM
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report the progress done at CENAM to build a thermal Cesium-beam frequency standard, with a short Ramsey cavity and optical pumping for atom detection and energy-state selection. In this paper we report our first observation of resonance pattern for the clock transition, in our setup.

articleTitle: High-accuracy voltage and current transmission by a four-coaxial cable
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The features of a four-coaxial line are recalled and an original compensation technique that reduces the voltage or current transmission error to below 10/sup -10/ at low frequency is presented. Active circuits suitable for the reproduction of EMFs or impressed currents of real generators within a high-precision measuring system even in loaded condition are shown.

articleTitle: Proposal of a test method for the linearity of the QHR
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Linearity test of I-V characteristic for QHR device at i=2 and i=4 has been performed by the dual frequency method for the purpose of linear resistor standard.

articleTitle: Effect of anomalously low voltage noise in measurement systems with cross-correlation signal processing
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: When two uncorrelated thermal noise sources with matched intensities are coupled to the inputs of two-channel noise measurement system, the cross-spectral density of output voltage fluctuations becomes anomalously low, provided the measurement time is long enough. Results of experimental observations of such effect along with its theoretical explanation are presented.

articleTitle: Precise measurements on dielectric reference liquids over the temperature range 5-50/spl deg/C using coaxial line methods
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper reports on a programme of traceable measurements of the complex permittivity of dielectric reference liquids from 100 MHz to 5 GHz over a temperature range of up to 5-50/spl deg/C using Vector Network Analysers (VNAs) and coaxial-line cells, including a new cell designed for Through-Reflect-Line (TRL) calibration.

articleTitle: A frequency measurement system for an optical frequency standard at 1.5 /spl mu/m
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We: are making a frequency measurement system for an optical frequency standard operating at 1.5 /spl mu/m region using a saturated absorption of the v/sub 1/+v/sub 3/ band of /sup 13/C/sub 2/H/sub 2/ molecule. After the first preliminary measurement reported at CPEM98, we have been improving the system to make it more accurate and reliable. The status report will be presented including preliminary results of the frequency measurement using a mode-locked fiber laser.

articleTitle: Influence of frequency errors in the variance of the cumulative histogram
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: In this paper the calculation of the variance in the number of counts of the cumulative histogram used for the characterization of ADCs with the histogram method is presented. All cases of frequency error, number of periods of the stimulus signal and number of samples are considered making this approach more general than the traditional one.

articleTitle: Ultra low temperature behaviour of a cryogenic vacuum gap capacitor
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A vacuum gap capacitor for operation at millikelvin temperatures has been designed, fabricated and tested. Below 500 mK the capacitance value exhibits a relative temperature dependence (dC/dT)C/sup -1/ that is smaller than 10/sup -9//mK. The long term relative stability is better than 5/spl middot/10/sup -6//day.

articleTitle: Development of fast-switching Nb/Al/Nb SNS junctions for the AC Josephson voltage standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report here the current development status of our Nb/Al/Nb SNS Josephson junctions for a programmable voltage standard. The morphology and the electrical parameters of these junctions are strongly dependent on the Al deposition rate. The RF and magnetic field behaviour is also reported, together with preliminary data about the uniformity and reproducibility of the series arrays made with this technology.

articleTitle: NRC-NIST intercomparison of power meter calibrations at 60 Hz and ranges up to 600 V, 100 A
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A number of international comparisons of power meter calibrations at power frequencies were conducted in the past, however, all of them were done at 120 V and 5 A. This intercomparison of power meter calibrations between the National Research Council of Canada and the National Institute of Standards and Technology, USA, was done to include voltage ranges up to 600 V, current ranges up to 100 A, and at power factors of 1.0, 0.5 lead and lag, and 0.0 lead and lag. The comparison was implemented by a transfer standard consisting of a modified commercial time-division multiplier type wattmeter based on a development at the National Research Council of Canada.

articleTitle: Extension of frequency atlas of molecular iodine at 532 nm
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Hyperfine structures of the R(122)35-0, P(84)33-0, P(104)34-0, P(55)32-0, and R(58)32-0 transitions of molecular iodine near 532 nm have been observed on the red end of the tuning range of the frequency-doubled Nd:YAG lasers. We have obtained excellent signal-to-noise ratios of the hyperfine structures by using modulation transfer spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Reliability design of a calibration laboratory automation software
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The objective of the following paper is to discuss the reliability improvement of an automated calibration laboratory software. For identification of reliability critical points several software designs and testing guidelines are discussed with the intention of achieving not only the minimum uncertainty but also the maximum reliability of the automation software.

articleTitle: Josephson voltage standards-a review
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This talk reviews the development and use of Josephson voltage standards (JVS) over the last 30 years, including classical DC standards, programmable standards based on binary weighted arrays, pulse-driven delta-sigma standards for AC waveform synthesis, and single-flux-quantum voltage multipliers.

articleTitle: Characterisitics of single junction thermal converters
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A recent analysis of the AC-DC difference (/spl delta/) of a single junction thermal converter (SJTC) affords the opportunity to obtain further insight into the behaviour of these devices. We show that higher order terms make a significant contribution to /spl delta/. While radiation is a significant heat loss, it has little effect on /spl delta/.

articleTitle: 100 kV DC voltage standard divider of the shielded type
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A shielded high-voltage divider equipped with a temperature control system has been developed for the highly precise measurement of high DC voltages of up to 100 kV. The measuring divider consists of 101 highly precise wire-wound resistors with a total resistance of about 1 G/spl Omega/ and has been set up in a compressed gas vessel under sulphur hexafluoride (SF/sub 6/). The measuring divider is accommodated in an electrode arrangement under potential control, in a homogeneous electrical field, temperature control being ensured by Peltier elements. The nominal scaling factors are 100:1 and 10000:1. The experimental investigation of all resistors and influence quantities as well as the shielded construction and the temperature control system have allowed an uncertainty of 2*10/sup -6/ (k=2) to be achieved.

articleTitle: Octofilar resistors with calculable frequency dependence
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We present the results of calculations of the frequency dependence of resistors consisting of eight parallel resistive elements similar in design to the common reversed quadrifilar resistor. At 12906 /spl Omega/ a commercial octofilar resistor has a smaller frequency dependence than a reversed quadrifilar resistor with comparable spacing but twice the element length.

articleTitle: Absolute quantum efficiency measurements using correlated photons: A study of systematics
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Correlated photons can be used to measure the quantum efficiency of photon counting photodetectors without ties to any externally calibrated standards. We present a study of the measurement systematics for the purpose of reducing the measurement uncertainties to the 0.1% level and developing a robust measurement protocol.

articleTitle: Magnetoresistive watt-converter for measurement active power in the frequency range of 20 Hz-20 kHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new 20 Hz-20 kHz magnetoresistive watt-converter has been constructed. It has less than 0.5% non-linearity in the power range up to 40 W and less than 0.5% change in sensitivity in the whole frequency band. The converter has complex sensitivity at the frequency of 1 kHz equal to 25.9 exp(j 0.0015) mV/w*.

articleTitle: An accurate calculation of the reference electric field nonuniformity
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Computer-aided calculation of the reference electric field nonuniformity in the electric field-meter calibration system is presented, which can help to lower the uncertainty of the reference field generation, and to reduce the traditionally large size of calibration systems.

articleTitle: A high-temperature superconducting transmission line for cryogenic electrical metrology applications
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper describes the design, realization, and testing of a high-temperature superconducting (HTS) transmission line structure for delivering calibrated dc and ac signals to a cryogenic test platform. The inclusion of the HTS transmission line in the signal path reduces parasitic wiring resistance, maintains thermal isolation within the cryostat, and transmits dc through audio frequency signals with minimal loss and degradation.

articleTitle: Cross-ratio method of reflection correction using waveguide air-lines in the millimeter wave range
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: It is shown that the cross-ratio method of reflection correction is applicable also to waveguides at millimeter waves when precision waveguide sections of well defined cross dimensions are used as reference air-line impedance standards. The uncertainty is small as the dimensions of the waveguides used are determined with low uncertainties.

articleTitle: Stability tests of three cryo-cooled sapphire oscillators
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We present frequency stability and phase noise results of three cryo-cooled sapphire oscillators. Technical designs include cryocooler integration, compensated sapphire/ruby combination, and new receiver with Pound frequency lock circuit.

articleTitle: A convenient calibration procedure of six-port reflectometers
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper presents a convenient calibration technique of the six port reflectometer requiring two standards. Measurement performance of this method is compared with the results obtained with an IEC R 900 waveguide six-port reflectometer using the LRL calibration method. Comparison results are given at 94 GHz showing the efficiency of the new method.

articleTitle: Novel probes and evaluation procedures providing pseudo-vector information
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: In this study novel near-field probes have been analyzed, optimized and constructed. Together with the developed numerical algorithm (a combination of a downhill simplex and Givens updating algorithm) it is possible to reconstruct the ellipse parameters and with that to gain not only information about the field amplitude but also information about the field polarization at any measured location. The developed probes and procedures greatly enhance the quality of the information used in the development and optimization phase of various antennas and transmitters in the microwave range.

articleTitle: Fundamental determination of the loss factor of 1 /spl mu/f capacitors at 1 kHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper presents a new measuring method which allows the loss factor of 1 /spl mu/F capacitors to be derived from the calculable time constant of a 200 /spl Omega/ AC resistor of bifilar structure. The method combines elements of the traditional bridge technique (Thomson balancing and Wagner earthing) with the digital synthesis of signals and their sampling using the discrete Fourier transform. The method allows the loss factor to be determined with an estimated standard uncertainty of measurement (k=1) of 2/spl times/10/sup -6/.

articleTitle: International comparison of a resistive divider at 100 kV DC
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Values of the voltage divider ratio of a dc high voltage divider, built and characterised by NML of Australia, were determined at PSB of Singapore, CMS of Taiwan, SCL of Hong Kong and JEMIC of Japan by the comparison method, under an APMP programme. The resistance values of the NML divider were also determined in the participating laboratories.

articleTitle: International comparison of 50/60 Hz power (1996-1999)
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An international comparison of 50/60 Hz power is described. The traveling standard was an electronic power transducer which was tested at 120 V, 5 A, 53 Hz, at five power factors (1.0, 0.5 lead, 0.5 lag, 0.0 lead, and 0.0 lag). Fifteen national metrology institutes from six metrology regions participated in the comparison.

articleTitle: Time transfer using GPS carrier phase with multi-channel common-view
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Time transfer using GPS carrier phase measurements based on dual-frequency multi-channel common-view techniques is presented. By using the ionosphere-free combination of the carrier phase and performing the single-difference, we can obtain the relationship between two hydrogen-maser clocks. Moreover, combining the sub-nanosecond results of the multi-channel common-view based on dual-frequency code observations with the single-difference calculations, we resolve the ambiguity of the single-difference equation for time transfer. The short-baseline tests with common hydrogen-maser clock show that our methodology has a frequency stability of a few parts in 10/sup 16/ for averaging times of one day.

articleTitle: Maintenance and development of the capacitance unit at CENAM
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Aiming to relating the Farad to the Ohm, reproduced at Centro Nacional de Metrologia (CENAM) by means of the Quantized Hall Effect (QHE), a development project was planed. The results of the construction of a capacitance bridge that constitutes the first step to achieve this objective are presented.

articleTitle: The single electron R-pump: First experiment
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We fabricated and tested the single electron R-pump, i.e., a three-junction Al circuit with on-chip Cr resistors. Due to the presence of the resistors (R>R/sub K/=h/e/sup 2//spl ap/25.8 k/spl Omega/), the accuracy of electron transfer in the R-pump can approach the level of /spl delta/I/I/spl sim/10/sup -8/. Preliminary results of experiment with the R-pump made at PTB are reported.

articleTitle: Single electron transistor with two gate inputs
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We fabricate a single electron tunneling (SET) transister, and add an extra electrode covering the whole surface. This extra electrode works well as another gate input with the effective gate capacitance of 2 aF, which is 1/80 of that of the on-chip gate (0.16 fF). Compared with the noises under the operation by the two gate input, it is found that the SET transistor with the extra gate operation becomes noisy more than one order of magnitude of that with the on-chip gate.

articleTitle: Progress in Josephson voltage standard development
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report recent progress in developing Josephson junction array voltage standards. A new way to realize a programmable voltage standard using externally shunted SIS junctions is tested with experiments and simulations. Further ideas in voltage standard development are presented.

articleTitle: Absolute measurement of hyperfine splittings of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ lines at h/spl lambda//spl ap/633 nm for improved wavelength standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: With the aid of two diode laser spectrometers around 633 nm, we report the measurement of the iodine hyperfine components of the R(60)8-4, R(125)9-4, P(54)8-4 transitions located -12 GHz from the classical red He-Ne laser stabilized on the R(127)11-5 transition of /sup 127/I/sub 2/, the P(33)6-3 transition roughly 1 GHz away, the P(39)6-3 transition 3.4 GHz above, and the R(59)8-4, P(53)8-4 transitions roughly 19 GHz above. The Doppler-free absorption signals were resolved using a third-harmonic detection technique and absolute frequency splittings by beat frequency techniques. The individual hyperfine transitions were linked by direct frequency measurements up to 16 GHz. The experimental uncertainty was typically below 8 kHz (<1.7/spl middot/10/sup -11/). First results on the strong group of transitions show a short-term stability better than that of the classical He-Ne laser, with a relative stability of 4/spl middot/10/sup -12/ for 1 s.

articleTitle: Laser-cooled /sup 87/Rb clock
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Preliminary measurements of the cold collision frequency shift in /sup 87/Rb fountain clocks have shown it to be much smaller than that in a Cs fountain. We will report our measurement of the cold collision shift in /sup 87/Rb, and on progress towards achieving high short-term stability in our Rb fountain.

articleTitle: Is linear regression good enough for determining bridge balance in precision high resistance measurements?
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The goodness of linear regression for determining the balance point of a bridge used in precision high resistance measurements is studied, and it is found that the technique may produce a large error. It is shown that, well-correlated data does not guarantee an accurate balance point to be obtained, and the accuracy depends on the sum of squared deviations of datapoints from their mean.

articleTitle: Precise current comparator for the calibration of high voltage standard transformers
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The development of a precise low-frequency current comparator and a fused silica tube capacitor standard for the calibration of high-voltage standard transformers is described. A comparison with a high-voltage standard transformer of the PTB was carried out using these devices; measurement results obtained are presented.

articleTitle: Further progress in relating the kilogram to h with the NPL watt balance
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: With the completed development of methods to align the coil with respect to magnetic flux, we believe the NPL moving-coil apparatus can relate the kilogram to Planck's constant to 1 in 10/sup 2/ in the near future.

articleTitle: Calibration of AC voltage
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper describes a modification to a present system used to calibrate AC/DC transfer to enable the calibration of AC voltage measuring instruments in the range 0.5 to 1000 V. The frequency range is up to 100 kHz above 100 V and 1 MHz at 100 V and below.

articleTitle: Report on the CCEM comparison of 10 pF capacitance standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper describes the recent Comite Consultatif d'Electricite et Magnetisme (CCEM) comparison of 10 pF capacitors. This comparison of electrical standards between the regional metrology organization will establish the relationship of the capacitance unit, the farad, for national metrology institutes from several metrology regions.

articleTitle: Current dependence measurement of resistance using a cryogenic constant current source with linear output
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We developed a cryogenic constant current source with linear output by using a cryogenic current comparator. When changing the current supplied to a resistor, nonlinear change of its voltage drop corresponds to current dependence of its resistance. We used a Josephson potentiometer with high linearity to measure the voltage drop.

articleTitle: The measurement of optical frequencies with mode-locked lasers
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have shown that the modes of a femtosecond mode-locked laser are distributed uniformly in frequency space and can be used like a ruler to measure large optical frequency differences. To measure absolute optical frequencies we use nonlinear optics for the conversion into a large frequency interval. Unlike the complex harmonic frequency chains used in the past this new approach uses only a few laser sources (ideally just one) and is nevertheless capable of measuring almost any optical frequency with the same set up. We applied the new technique to determine the absolute frequencies of the cesium D/sub 1/ line at 335 THz, of several components in I/sub 2/ around 563 THz, the sharp /sup 115/In/sup +/5s/sup 21/S/sub 0/-5s5p/sup 3/P/sub 0/ transition at 1267 THz and the hydrogen 1S-2S transition at 2466 THz.

articleTitle: Fast reversed dc measurements on thermal converters using a SINIS Josephson junction array
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An array of 7492 SINIS Josephson junctions was used to generate fast reversed dc (FRDC) voltages of approx. 1.1 V for the study of thermoelectric effects in planar multijunction thermal converters (PMJTC). A bias current source for fast reversing with a frequency of up to 10 kHz has been designed. First measurements with a PMJTC have shown a slope in the FRDC-DC voltage transfer difference versus reversing frequency of about 10/sup -8//Hz. Regression to zero frequency allows to the FRDC-DC transfer difference to be determined with an uncertainty of less than 0.1 /spl mu/V/V.

articleTitle: Toward absolute determination in NRLM proto-type superconducting magnetic levitation system for the future replacement of kilogram
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Studies on residual subject such as a Meissner effect at intensive part and a correction for the attitude error of the floating body toward absolute determination in the NRLM proto-type superconducting magnetic levitation system are in progress.

articleTitle: A generalised treatment of the calibration and measurement for vector indicating microwave reflectometers
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper gives a generalised treatment of the calibration and measurement of vector-indicating microwave reflectometers. The reflection coefficient is treated as a complex measurand with an elliptical region of uncertainty. The reflectometer calibration is treated as (i) a deterministic problem, and (ii) an overdetermined problem employing generalised distance regression.

articleTitle: Direct RF to optical frequency measurements with a femtosecond laser comb
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: By spanning an optical octave (>300 THz) with a broadened femtosecond laser frequency comb, we directly measure optical frequency standards at 1064/532 nm, 633 nm and 778 nm in terms of the microwave frequency that controls the comb spacing.

articleTitle: Development of an ac-dc thermal converter at millivolt level operating at cryogenic temperature
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A device for the measurements of ac-dc transfer difference at millivolt level is under development at IEN. In this device a Cr heater, Nb leads and a Nb transition edge thermometer have been deposited by evaporation on a silicon nitride (SiN) membrane. Analysis on the possible effects on the ac-dc transfer difference and first experimental tests show the possibility of high accuracy direct measurements at the level of 1 mV.

articleTitle: North American interlaboratory comparison of 10 V Josephson voltage standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An interlaboratory comparison of Josephson voltage standards has been made among 16 national, industrial, and military standards laboratories in North America and 1 in Germany. The comparison was made at 10 V using a set of four transfer Zener reference standards. A pivot laboratory made measurements at the beginning, end, and at 9 other times during the comparison. The measured differences and their uncertainties are used to establish a table of equivalence between all pairs of participants.

articleTitle: Intercomparison of resistance standards with calculable frequency dependence for the characterisation of quantum Hall devices
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have constructed AC/DC transfer resistance standards with nominal values of 12906.4 /spl Omega/. The design of these resistors follows Gibbings principles [1963]. The resistors differ considerably since bifilar, quadrifilar, and octafilar units have been built. In addition the length of the quadrifilar units was varied.

articleTitle: 100 Ohm transfer standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new 100 /spl Omega/ transfer standard has been built and placed in service at VTT Automation. The temperature of the resistor is maintained at 30.72/spl deg/C where the temperature coefficient is zero. The daily variation in temperature is less than /spl plusmn/0.005/spl deg/C. The temperature during transportation is about 0.06/spl deg/C less than the nominal value and it can be hold for about 40 hours. The behavior of the standard was verified in the resistance comparison between VTT (Finland), PTB (Germany), BIPM (International) and BNM-LCIE (France) in November-December 1998. The result indicates that the variation of the standard during the transportation is less than 6.10/sup -9/.

articleTitle: Calibration of HF thermal voltage converters using an asymmetrical Tee
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The paper discusses systematic errors in the AC-DC difference determination resulting from the comparison of thermal voltage converters with different input connectors. Tests of the internal Tee of the calorimetric thermal voltage converter, as well as, two asymmetrical Tees, with GR-874 and type-N arms, are presented.

articleTitle: Recent developments in BIPM voltage standard comparisons
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The BIPM carries out a number of comparisons of DC voltage standards with national metrology institutes. These take the form of on-site comparisons of Josephson standards or bilateral comparisons using travelling standards based on Zener diodes. This paper describes some of the new procedures used in both types of comparisons and presents some results of five recent BIPM key comparisons.

articleTitle: Transport behaviour of commercially available 100 /spl Omega/ standard resistors
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The transport behaviour of five commercially available 100 /spl Omega/ standard resistors from three different manufacturers is evaluated by sending them to eleven national metrological institutes (NMIs) where they are calibrated against a resistance standard based on the quantized Hall effect (QHE). The results of these measurements are presented.

articleTitle: New group resistance standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The standards are based on the groups of metal-foil resistors connected by four-terminal junctions. Their values are chosen approximately in the middle of the range where the most accurate measurements are made in practice. In manufacturing, the connection error is reduced by the method of virtual currents. The stability of resistors determines the value of standards with an error of about 0.02 ppm during 6 months between their measurements using the QHR, The new 1 Ohm group standard may be used for direct link between the voltage of 1 V and the current of 1 A.

articleTitle: Accurate nuclear transition data determined by prompt (n,/spl gamma/)-spectrometry
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Prompt (n,/spl gamma/)-spectrometry is an on-line measurement for the determination of characteristics of nuclei (atomic masses, cross sections, level schemes, etc.) and nondestructive investigation of the isotopic composition (and, therefore, of the element composition) of any sample. The thermal neutrons are captured in the sample according to their isotope-specific cross sections and cause an high internal excitation of the nuclei concerned. This leads to an immediate rearrangement of the nucleons in a new state most favourable with respect to energy, and the excess energy is dissipated by prompt emission of electromagnetic radiation in the form of characteristic /spl gamma/-quanta. The process takes place for all isotopes (contrary to the neutron activation analysis), is nondestructive and has no need for sample preparation (contrary to the mass spectrometry). Moreover it is independent of the sample dimensions and its state of aggregation.

articleTitle: Electro-optic sensor for measurement of DC fields in the presence of space charge
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The paper presents theoretical analysis and experimental verification of an electro-optic sensor for DC electric fields in space charge environment. Both unipolar and bipolar charge environments were investigated. In both cases the sensor output is linearly dependent on the measured electric field and independent of the density of space charge.

articleTitle: A bi-directional interferometric frequency discriminator for low noise microwave applications
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: New interferometric frequency discriminators (FD) for frequency stabilization of microwave oscillators are examined. Alternative topologies to the standard interferometric readout are presented. The new readouts are arranged in a bi-directional configuration. In this configuration, microwaves pass in both directions through each arm of the interferometer. The coupling to the resonator is adjusted to maximize the frequency discriminator sensitivity. The sensitivity is compared with that for the conventional interferometric FD and found to be 6 dB greater. No circulator is required within the interferometer, thus eliminating its phase noise contribution.

articleTitle: Evaluation of major frequency shifts in an optically pumped cesium beam frequency standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The accuracy evaluation of the optically pumped cesium beam frequency standard with a 37-cm long Ramsey cavity, KRISS-1, is being performed. Some major frequency shifts are evaluated; e.g., second-order Zeeman and Doppler shifts, cavity pulling, Rabi pulling, etc. The overall uncertainty is expected to be at the low 10/sup -13/ level in the KRISS-1.

articleTitle: Towards traceability of the direct calibration method to the cal kit standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The Direct Calibration Method for characterisation of three-port devices is presented. Formulas for derivation of the measurement uncertainty are provided, which relate the DUT parameters to the characterisation of the calibration standards. Traceability is obtained from a certificate of calibration or, alternatively, from the manufacturer's specifications.

articleTitle: Determination of the Avogadro constant from precision density measurements on a silicon sphere
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Density measurements with relative uncertainty of 1/spl times/10/sup -7/ have been made on a highly polished 1 kg single crystal silicon sphere. The molar mass, crystal quality and lattice parameter have been measured elsewhere, enabling a determination of the Avogadro constant to be made. The purpose is to obtain a definition of the kilogram in terms of a specific number of /sup 12/C atoms.

articleTitle: Fiber-coupled and monolithic cryogenic optical resonators
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have developed a fiber coupled cryogenic optical sapphire resonator for the frequency stabilization of a Nd:YAG laser. With this method a frequency instability of 2/spl middot/10/sup -15/ for /spl tau/=1 hour integration time has been achieved. This is among the lowest values ever obtained for optical oscillators. We also present a new approach to test the time-independence of the fine structure constant, based on the use of a single monolithic resonator. Preliminary results on the development of suitable resonators are described.

articleTitle: Characterization of four-terminal-pair resistance standards: a comparison of measurements and theory
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Coaxial straight-wire resistance standards with calculable frequency dependence have been used to tie alternating-current (AC) measurements to direct-current (DC) measurements of resistance. Coaxial standards of values 100 /spl Omega/ and 1000 /spl Omega/ are compared with each other and with other resistance standards at several frequencies up to 15920 Hz using AC bridges.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of DBR diode laser against Cs absorption lines at 852 nm using the modulation transfer method
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report preliminary results of the frequency stabilization of DBR-diode lasers to saturated absorption of Cs D-line by means of the modulation transfer spectroscopy method. From the experimental analysis of the signal to noise ratio, a relative frequency stability of the order of /spl ap/10/sup -12//spl middot//spl tau//sup - 1/2 / should be achieved.

articleTitle: Responsivity calibration methods for 365 nm irradiance meters
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Two detector-based responsivity calibration methods have been compared at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) for UV irradiance meters in the 365 nm spectral region. Both methods are based on an electrical substitution High Accuracy Cryogenic Radiometer (HACR), but utilize different facilities and transfer standards. One facility is a monochromator-based, spectral power responsivity measuring system utilizing an aperture scanning method, while the second is a tunable laser and integrating sphere source system using a light-trapping silicon transfer detector with a known aperture area. The first comparison by NIST of these two fundamentally different methods agreed to 1% to 2% near the peak and long wavelength side of the bandpass curves which is comparable to their expanded (k=2) uncertainties.

articleTitle: Use of precise digital voltmeters for ac voltage measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The possibility of using high-resolution digital voltmeters for ac voltage measurements at a frequency of about 16 Hz is presented. The method for the determination of correction factors in phase difference measurements with two synchronised voltmeters is described, and a level of uncertainty of 0,1 /spl mu/rad is achieved.

articleTitle: On a nonimaging optics approach to diode lasers collimation
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper discusses applications of a class of reflecting optical components, called Compound Parabolic Concentrators (CPC) to diode lasers. Their performances and design are evaluated at the aid of ray-tracing methods. The simulation will report conclusions on the efficiency of CPC and compare its performances against those of standard optics.

articleTitle: Silicon molar volume discrepancy: perfection of the NRLM crystal [for Avogadro constant determination]
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A large discrepancy was found in the molar volume of silicon used to determine Avogadro constant. Voids are suspected to cause the difference in the molar volume. Laser scattering tomography, secco-etching, electron spin resonance and X-ray topography have been applied to Japanese silicon to detect voids but no voids were observed in the crystal.

articleTitle: Automated self-calibration resistive divider for 10 V to 1 kV
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have built a guarded resistive divider with 10:1 and 100:1 ratios for voltages under 1 kV. This divider performs self-calibrations by an automated guarded Wheatstone bridge method. The ratios different from those of a series-parallel divider are sub ppm and 1 ppm at 10:1 and 100:1 ratios respectively.

articleTitle: Applications of coupled dielectric resonators using SrTiO/sub 3/ pucks: tunable resonators and novel thermometry
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The combination of very low loss dielectric single crystal materials with a HTS shielding enclosure provides high Q resonators in the temperature range 40-70 K which show great promise for frequency standard applications. We report electronic tuning of a sapphire dielectric puck resonator by using a SrTiO/sub 3/ tuning element situated in the evanescent field region outside the sapphire puck. In addition when the sapphire and SrTiO/sub 3/ elements act as weakly coupled resonators, the resonant frequency becomes a very sensitive function of temperature, allowing the possibility of very high resolution thermometry.

articleTitle: Characteristic impedance of standard air line
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A closed exact form and its approximation of the characteristic impedance of a lossy coaxial line with a thick outer conductor are presented. The characteristic impedance of a coaxial line calculated theoretically using dimensions measured by air-gauging system are compared to the measurement results using the Gamma method for a 3.5 mm standard air line of 15 cm long.

articleTitle: A W-band spectrometer for precision dielectric measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new spectrometer for the precision measurement of dielectric permittivity and loss tangent is presented. The new instrument is capable of providing the high resolution data for the first time over an extended W-band (68-118 GHz) frequencies for specimens with large range of absorption values, including highly absorbing specimens which otherwise would not be possible. A novel technique based on the unbalanced bridge is developed for the measurement of the phase of the wave passed through the specimen in free space (quasi-optical) with reference provided by a waveguide arm. Specially constructed precision waveguide and quasi-optical components allowed reliable broad band operation. A number of common dielectrics are measured and results are compared with previously reported data.

articleTitle: Observation and temperature measurement of the sympathetically cooled ions in an rf trap
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The barium ions are trapped with the laser-cooled magnesium ions simultaneously in an rf trap and cooled sympathetically. Sympathetically cooled ions are one of the candidates of accurate optical frequency standard. The barium ions are ionized by the charge transfer with the magnesium ions for avoiding the loss due to the shallow trapping potential. The temperature of the barium ions is measured and the effect of the sympathetic cooling is observed. It is also found that the application of the ionization by the charge transfer to other ion species is possible.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of an internal-mirror 1.523 /spl mu/m longitudinal Zeeman He-Ne laser
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The polarization properties of an internal-mirror 1.523-/spl mu/m He-Ne laser under an axial magnetic field were investigated. When the magnetic field was around 12 mT, we could stabilize the laser frequency at either the center of gain profile or the symmetric two-mode position, and the stability achieved was better than 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Measuring the ramp linearity of extremely linear frequency ramps using a fractional dual loop structure
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A dual loop synthesizer concept based on fractional divider techniques for measuring highly linear analog frequency ramps is presented. Due to the excellent sensitivity of the measurement set-up relative nonlinearities as low as 10/sup -9/ are ascertainable. The measurements obtained with the prototype circuit are shown. They prove the expected high sensitivity.

articleTitle: To increase reliability of certification of standard geodetic bases
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The problem of metrological assurance of means of distance measurement is considered. The method of certification of linear geodetic bases by means of wave measure for distance measurement, as alternative of using Väisälä interferometer is proposed. The block diagram and principle of operation of instrument, which the wave measure for distance measurement is used as a working measure.

articleTitle: Measurements of volume and density of the new IMGC silicon standard [for Avogadro constant determination]
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The IMGC has developed volume-density standards in the form of single-crystal silicon spheres within the project for the determination of the Avogadro constant. A new sphere of nearly perfect form is going to be available, made of high-purity and near-perfect silicon single-crystal. The absolute determination of its mass and volume is presented together with the expected improvements. The new standard will be then intercompared with similar artifacts within a joint international project coordinated through the WG on the Avogadro constant of the CCM.

articleTitle: Precise measurement of dielectric constants of liquids using the principle of the cross capacitor
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A precise measurement system with very simple electrodes for non-contacting measurement of dielectric characteristics of liquids has been developed. This forms a cross capacitor based on the Thompson-Lampard theorem. Over a temperature range of 25-100/spl deg/C, the dielectric constants can be precisely measured with uncertainty less than /spl plusmn/0.02-0.05%.

articleTitle: Characterization of the travelling standard for an international comparison of AC-DC transfer difference in the millivolt range
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An international comparison of AC-DC transfer difference in the mV-range started in the beginning of year 2000, EUROMET Project 464, with SP as pilot laboratory. The result of the characterisation of the travelling standard is reported. In order to fulfil the requirements the standard was modified on certain characteristics.

articleTitle: International comparison of power measurements at 62 GHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A BIPM international key-comparison of power measurements at 62 GHz (GT-RF/95-1) has been carried out between four national metrology institutes. The BNM-LCIE acted as pilot laboratory. The results show very good agreement in measuring the effective efficiency and the magnitude of reflection coefficient for the unique IEC R620 waveguide thermistor mount involved in the comparison.

articleTitle: An automated multiharmonic source-pull/load-pull system based on six-port techniques
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have improved our existing Source-Pull/Load-Pull setup to allow independent active tuning, both at fundamental and second harmonic frequency, of the load and source impedance of the device-under-test (DUT). We will present experimental results to validate the calibration procedure and to show the accuracy of the measurements.

articleTitle: Automatic microcalorimeter system for broad band power measurement in 75-110 GHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A system, which automatically measures an effective efficiency of a bolometer mount (BM) in the frequency range of 75-110 GHz (W-band), was developed. It consists of a dry mono-load microcalorimeter and a broadband signal source. An automatic measuring algorithm was newly devised, and it has merit to shorten measuring time. Measurements of effective efficiency were carried out in the full band by 1 GHz intervals and results have shown the possibility of broadband calibration using this system.

articleTitle: Kerr-lens mode-locked lasers as ultra-low noise microwave sources
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We propose a novel application of Kerr-lens mode-locked (KLM) lasers: ultra-low-noise frequency conversion from the optical to the microwave region. Using self-heterodyning techniques we show that the quantum-limited pulse timing noise level of these lasers can be substantially smaller than the noise floor generated by state-of-the-art microwave oscillators. Thus, after conversion of the output pulse train of these lasers into a microwave signal, it may be used as an interrogation signal for modern microwave frequency standards like Cs-fountain clocks, thus improving the frequency noise performance of these devices.

articleTitle: Sub-Doppler atomic velocities for an optical frequency standard by Maxwell's demon cooling
