publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report on a novel cooling scheme that allows sub-Doppler cooling of atoms previously subject to the Doppler limit. The method was applied to enhance the fringe contrast in an optical Ca frequency standard.

articleTitle: A microprocessor based electronic high performance capacitor
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A simple but accurate and stable system for realizing a high performance large capacitance capacitor is studied. By compensating a usual 100.3 nF capacitor with a 100.0 pF standard capacitor using a microprocessor, a 100.0 nF capacitor, with performance as good as the standard capacitor, has been obtained.

articleTitle: Improvements of the NMi VSL HF AC-DC transfer facilities
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper reports recent developments of the VSL high frequency AC-DC transfer facilities. For the calculable HF AC-DC standard, figures are given on the long-term stability and consistency between other users. Furthermore, improvements of the measurement set-up (frequency and voltage range and stability) and the RF voltage control are discussed.

articleTitle: High resistance comparison among KRISS, VNIIM and NIM
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: In a high resistance comparison among KRISS, VNIIM and NIM, the relative resistance values of measurement results agreed well within 2 ppm in 10 megohm and 5 ppm in 1 gigohm. Also, relative combined standard uncertainties of the three institutes is 4.9 ppm in 10 megohm and 11.6 ppm in 1 gigohm.

articleTitle: Comparison of complex scattering coefficient measurements of a microwave step attenuator
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper presents results obtained from a recent measurement comparison exercise of complex scattering coefficients of a microwave step attenuator. The results obtained by the eight participating laboratories are summarised in terms of the between-laboratory reproducibility. Multivariate robust statistical techniques are used to summarise the complex-valued data.

articleTitle: Microwave interaction of temperature compensation thermistors in thermistor mounts
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: At some frequencies, both the calibration factor and the reflection coefficient of some thermistor mounts have been found to depend on whether or not the temperature compensation thermistors are energised.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of a 1.54 /spl mu/m DFB-laser diode to Doppler-free lines of acetylene
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report on results of the stabilization of a distributed feedback (DFB) laser diode to Doppler-free saturated absorption lines of acetylene /sup 13/C/sub 2/H/sub 2/ using an external build-up cavity. A FM-spectroscopic method is utilized to obtain signals with reduced sensitivity to frequency fluctuations between the laser and the cavity.

articleTitle: Derivation of an electronic equivalent of QHE devices
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A network with only resistors and unity gain amplifiers has been proven to be equivalent to the Ricketts and Kemeny (1988) electrical model of multiterminal QHE devices. This new circuit allows to simulate QHE behavior both by means of usual electronic circuit analysis software or even by direct measurement on a physical model, but its applicability is limited to devices in perfect quantization state. There are instances, e.g. in the analysis of AC QHE, where a model with nonzero longitudinal resistance is needed. In the following we present an enhanced electronic equivalent, suited to model QHE devices with any value of longitudinal resistance, and discuss its properties. The circuit is shown to belong to a class of nonreciprocal electrical elements (gyrators), that can be regarded as generalized equivalents of Hall effect devices, thus setting a general framework for the derivation of electrical models of QHE.

articleTitle: Development of a compact acetylene optical frequency standard at 1.5 /spl mu/m
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have developed an optical frequency standard at 1.5 /spl mu/m based on the acetylene overtone transitions. We have realized the frequency stability of about 2/spl times/10/sup -13/ and the frequency accuracy of about 10/sup -10/. A compact and portable frequency standard can be realized with the use of a DFB laser and a high-finesse Fabry-Perot cavity absorption cell.

articleTitle: Whispering gallery method of measuring complex permittivity in highly anisotropic materials
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The Whispering Gallery (WG) mode method to measure complex permittivity is applied to the highly anisotropic material rutile. In an isotropic or slightly anisotropic material standard WG mode families exist and may be measured to accurately determine the complex permittivity tensor components. In this paper we show that the standard WG mode families in general do not always exist in an anisotropic material. This phenomenon limits the applicability of the WG mode method. However, we identify a new type of WG mode and show that it may be used to help determine the tensor components of the complex permittivity.

articleTitle: Characterization of a cold cesium source for PARCS: Primary Atomic Reference Clock in Space
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The PARCS (Primary Atomic Reference Clock in Space) project is a joint NIST JPL venture aimed at placing a Cs atomic clock aboard the International Space Station. This orbiting clock will achieve high accuracies in part due to the long Ramsey times afforded by the microgravity environment. The clock will allow a wide range of precision tests of fundamental physics including relativity theory. Our group at NIST is performing experimental studies of a "prototype" cold Cs source based on launching atoms from optical molasses. The results of our work will be applied to the design and construction of a robust, space qualified device. Additionally, this work is important for the development of future Cs fountains. We describe our apparatus, the present state of our experimental work, and planned improvements.

articleTitle: Measurements of antenna characteristics over different conducting planes
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Measurement of dipole antennas by three-antenna method is evaluated by the comparison of the different types of open-area test site. These results show that the repeatability of the derived antenna factors is within /spl plusmn/0.3 dB for the fixed element dipole antennas in the case of the same height measurement.

articleTitle: Potentiometric calibration of dc voltage- and resistance-ratios up to 1000 V
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: 1:1 ratio of a divider's resistance up to 100 k/spl Omega/ at 100 V and 10:1 voltage ratio up to 1 kV can be accurately measured by a potentiometric method. Common-mode potential effect on voltmeter offset is removed by reversing whole divider for high voltage measurement. The best relative measurement uncertainty (k=1) was estimated to be less than 0.02/spl times/10/sup -6/ for 10 V/10 V or 10 k/spl Omega//10 k/spl Omega/.

articleTitle: Microwave properties of large SINIS series arrays for Josephson voltage standards of intrinsic stability
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Series arrays of several thousands of overdamped SINIS junctions have been fabricated for programmable voltage standards. The arrays can be operated with low microwave power, since the major part of the microwave power is generated by the junctions itself. The operation of the arrays and the formation of Shapiro steps is discussed.

articleTitle: Uncertainty evaluation of GPS common-view time transfer and frequency stability measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An experiment was carried out to determine the uncertainty of GPS common-view time transfers. The receivers operated on different tracking schedules for some satellites. We found that standard deviation of about 20 ns was attainable even when there were several minutes difference in tracking schedule for some satellites. A system developed for characterizing long- and short-term frequency stability of atomic clocks is also described. Measurement uncertainties of the system were also evaluated to establish traceability to UTC.

articleTitle: Improved value of the fine structure constant obtained from the electron g-2
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper reports improvement of the value of the fine structure constant /spl alpha/ by an extensive evaluation of the /spl alpha//sup 4/ term of the electron anomalous magnetic moment a/sub e/. This will enable us to obtain a value of /spl alpha/ with a precision exceeding 1 part in 10/sup 9/ when new measurements of a/sub e/ become available.

articleTitle: Traceable measurements of the magnetic susceptibility of weakly-magnetic mass standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Magnetic forces can adversely affect precise weighings. A systematic investigation is aimed at verifying a magnetic susceptometer and its attendant theory by measurement on a variety of weakly-magnetised objects of different materials over a range of relative permeabilities between 1.0013 and 1.2, including novel permeability standards.

articleTitle: The UWA/PTB optical synthesizer: an update
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper reports on the continuing development of a coherent optical synthesizer, based upon a combination of optical frequency-interval division, and an optical comb generated by a mode-locked laser. We report on the synthesizer design, as well as presenting the measured stability of the crucial elements. Based on these measurements, we estimate that the overall fractional frequency stability of the synthesizer will be in the range of 10/sup -15///spl tau/, where /spl tau/ is the integration time of the measurement.

articleTitle: Wavelength standard in 543 nm and the corresponding /sup 127/I/sub 2/ hyperfine transitions
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report on the features of our compact iodine-stabilized 543 nm He-Ne lasers and the corresponding /sup 127/I/sub 2/ hyperfine transitions. The stability, reproducibility and resettability are investigated; the frequency intervals of the resolved hyperfine peaks are measured: thus, the corresponding hyperfine constants are determined, and the linewidth of each main line is measured; the features of the suggested wavelength standard line b/sub 10/ are investigated in detail.

articleTitle: Frequency dependence of quantized charge transport with surface acoustic waves
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The surface acoustic wave (SAW) induced quantized transport of electrons has been studied in an extended frequency range. Using electron beam lithography, Interdigital Transducers (IDTs) of different types have been designed and fabricated for frequencies of up to 9 GHz. Successful operation of the devices has been possible up to 5 GHz.

articleTitle: An asymetrical sensor for simultaneous electric and magnetic field measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Two sensors are proposed in this paper: a uniaxial sensor and a biaxial one, Each of them allows the simultaneous measurement of the magnetic and electric field close to a ground plane. They are characterized by the fact that only the sensitive element-a very simple, small-sized halfloop, allowing both E and H measurements-is introduced in the region containing the field of interest.

articleTitle: High-resolution spectroscopy of the 435 nm /sup 2/S/sub 1/2/-/sup 2/D/sub 3/2/ transition in trapped /sup 171/Yb/sup +/
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Single /sup 171/Yb ions are laser cooled in a miniature radiofrequency trap. We demonstrate high-resolution spectroscopy of the potential frequency-standard reference transition from the F=0 ground-state sublevel to the metastable /sup 2/D/sub 3/2/ (F=2, m/sub F/=0) level at a wavelength of 435 nm. Presently achieved minimum linewidths are in the range of 80 Hz.

articleTitle: A long term time and frequency transfer by GPS CP over a very long baseline
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A time and frequency transfer experiment by GPS carrier phase has been set up over the Atlantic. This paper focuses on the long term behaviour of the technique and on its performances in comparison with well established methods. In particular, the results are confronted to those obtained by TWSTFT over the same baseline.

articleTitle: Realization of a DC SQUID picovoltmeter
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A picovoltmeter based on a DC SQUID has been developed for the direct comparison between Josephson standards (PROVOLT project). The experimental results show a excellent agreement with the theory. An equivalent noise of 0.7 pV//spl radic/Hz is achieved in the white noise region, which extends down to 10 mHz.

articleTitle: Determining the specific total power loss and other properties of soft magnetic materials at frequencies up to 100 kHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: When extending the measurement of soft magnetic materials to frequencies above 10 kHz, existing international standards cannot be used. One measurement condition specified is control of the secondary waveform. The effect of secondary distortions on the power loss is reported and a control method for high frequency work is introduced.

articleTitle: Measurement of complex voltage ratios by means of precise digital voltmeters
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The possibility of using high-resolution digital voltmeters for voltage ratio measurements at a frequency of 16 Hz is presented. The method is used for the determination of unknown parasitic capacitances in a voltage divider. The voltage ratio and phase differences are measured in some cases with 0,1 ppm and 0,1 /spl mu/rad uncertainty, respectively.

articleTitle: Frequency modulation spectroscopy of iodine at 532 nm using a vibrating mirror
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We demonstrate a simple and low cost method to observe the frequency modulation (FM) saturated absorption spectrum of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ at 532 nm. We use a vibrating mirror with modulation frequency of 570 kHz to modulate the laser frequency. Preliminary result is shown for the iodine P(54) 32-0 line.

articleTitle: Measurements of single electron transistor devices combined with a CCC: progress report
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: BNM-LCIE is developing a current standard based on single electron transistor (SET) pumps. The paper gives an overview of the experimental set-up. The latest results, including the testing of a high gain current comparator (CCC) and first measurements of a SET, are presented.

articleTitle: NRC-PTB intercomparison of voltage transformer calibration systems for high voltage
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An intercomparison of voltage transformer calibration systems was performed at the PTB high voltage laboratory. A "portable" current-comparator-based voltage transformer calibration system of NRC was compared with PTB's voltage-divider-based system, using a reference multi-ratio inductive voltage transformer with voltage ratios up to (400 kV//spl radic/3)/(100 V//spl radic/3) as a transfer standard. At frequencies of 50 Hz and 60 Hz with a resistive burden of 10 k/spl Omega/ and test voltages of 20% up to 120% of rated voltage, the test results of the two different methods at all ratios were found to differ by no more than 15/spl times/10/sup -6/ for the voltage ratio and 30 /spl mu/rad for the phase displacement.

articleTitle: Measurement of the collisional frequency shift in a /sup 87/Rb fountain
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We describe the operation of a laser cooled /sup 87/Rb frequency standard and present a measurement of the /sup 87/Rb ground state hyperfine frequency with a relative accuracy of 2.2/spl times/10/sup -15/, by comparison with Cs fountains primary standards. The measured frequency is 6834682610.904333(17) Hz. We present in detail our measurements of the cavity pulling effect and frequency shift induced by cold collisions. We compare it with the most recent predictions of collision theories. The collisional frequency shift is at least 30 times smaller than for /sup 133/Cs. This opens the way towards accuracies in the 10/sup -16/ range together with an excellent frequency stability for cold atom microwave standards. In addition, the comparisons between our Cs and Rb fountains lead to a test of the fine structure constant /spl alpha/ variations with time at the level of 7/spl times/10/sup -15/ per year.

articleTitle: Recent measurements of single electron transport in surface acoustic wave devices at the NPL
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The quantized acoustoelectric current (QAC) induced by a surface acoustic wave in a one-dimensional channel, offers the possibility of a quantum current standard. We report on the accuracy and flatness of the QAC for several plateaux and demonstrate an empirical relationship between the current error and plateaux slopes. The temperature dependence of the QAC is also discussed.

articleTitle: Measurement uncertainty in the 1/f noise region: Zener voltage standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The measurement uncertainty is studied in terms of the Allan variance when the uncertainty is limited by 1/f noise. The deadtime in measurements determines the time scale of best measurement uncertainty. About ten equally spaced samples seem to map the noise spectrum well enough and no uncertainty improvement results from further averaging. The voltage difference of two Zener standards in the frequency band 10/sup -6/-10/sup 3/ Hz was studied and closely 1/f behaviour was detected. The noise floor of one Zener is about 70 nV.

articleTitle: Reinforcing a telephone synchrony network in Mexico using the GPS common-view technique
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: In this paper we show how the Common View (CV) Technique, a simple but powerful tool, was the better solution for TELMEX, the largest telephone company in Mexico, to improve its synchrony network in order to give a better and reliable telephonic public services. The CV links, between the main telephone centrals and the National Metrology Center in Mexico, CENAM supports and strengthens this synchrony network. Experimental results of the electromagnetic environment studies and those obtained from the receiver's calibration, at TELMEX stations are reported.

articleTitle: Measurement of time delay for a transmission line in frequency domain
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper describes the measurement of the time delay for a transmission line using a frequency discriminator to demodulate a carrier with FM modulation in frequency domain. The trace of demodulation signal shows the dip points. These dip points appear at the frequency multiples of 1/Td. The measurement results of the frequency domain are compared with the time domain method.

articleTitle: Frequency uncertainty of I/sub 2/-stabilized Nd:YAG lasers
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have established two portable I/sub 2/-stabilized Nd:YAG lasers for the investigation of the uncertainty of the laser frequency. A third I/sub 2/-stabilized Nd:YAG laser is now in progress. A new experiment measuring the absolute optical frequency of the 532 nm I/sub 2/-stabilized Nd:YAG laser referred to Rb-2-photon transitions is proposed and being developed.

articleTitle: Development of optical frequency standards based upon the /sup 2/S/sub 1/2/-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ transition in /sup 88/Sr/sup +/ and /sup 87/Sr/sup +/
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Optical frequency standards, based on the 674 nm transition in /sup 88/Sr/sup +/ and /sup 87/Sr/sup +/ are being developed. Zeeman components in two /sup 88/Sr/sup +/ traps were compared, with stabilities of 100 Hz measured at a few tens of seconds. /sup 87/Sr/sup +/ offers "clock" transitions with no first-order Zeeman shifts and laser cooled /sup 87/Sr/sup +/ ions have been observed.

articleTitle: Reconstruction and preliminary tests of the NIST electronic kilogram experiment
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The NIST electronic kilogram experiment is being completely rebuilt into a vacuum chamber within a specially designed laboratory room. Major renovations include reference mass positioning equipment, structural alignment flexures, and a redesigned inductive coil. The goal is less than 10 nW/W uncertainty. Preliminary data on measurement capabilities are expected.

articleTitle: Design of Nd:YAG/KTP laser at 532 nm [for displacement interferometry and frequency standard]
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A diode-pumped solid-state Nd:YAG laser with frequency doubling in a KTP crystal radiating at 532 nm has been designed for use in laser displacement interferometry and in a secondary frequency standard. The third-harmonic signals of the transitions of hyperfine structure of molecular iodine have been observed.

articleTitle: The Stark effect on the HFS of Cs atoms: application to blackbody radiation shift
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The purpose of present work is to develop a theory of higher-order Stark effect and blackbody radiation shift in Cs atoms. The results are compared with high-precision theoretical data and measurements.

articleTitle: Measurement of the frequency dependence of a single-electron tunneling capacitance standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: In the context of a proposed new capacitance standard based on counting electrons, we discuss a method to investigate its frequency dependence. We describe measurements of this frequency dependence using a technique that involves the same single-electron tunneling devices used in the capacitance standard.

articleTitle: Metrological quality of measured and evaluated values using automated measuring systems
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The present paper addresses issues related with the metrological performance of automated measuring systems (AMSs) and points out some possibilities opened in that domain by the increased ease of use and measurement throughput of such systems over nonautomated ones.

articleTitle: Bulk and edge phenomena in AC quantum Hall effect?
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We investigated the AC quantum Hall effect of several GaAs-based samples. The influence of temperature, current, and frequency was measured and seems to be caused by bulk and edge phenomena.

articleTitle: Gravitational force-a possible noise source of Zener standard under humidity change?
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Recently, we observed the Zener standard's 1.018 V output has a higher fluctuation when there is a change of humidity compared with measurements at stable humidity. The results show a periodic fluctuation pattern that can be correlated with the time when tide changes. This correlation suggested that the gravitational force may be affecting the Zener standard output voltage.

articleTitle: Traceability of national standard of frequency and its distribution in Slovenia
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Traceability of time and frequency in Republic of Slovenia is described. At present traceability to UTC is established by multichannel GPS comparison to UTC (IEN). A study on establishing traceability to UTC via UTC (USNO) is taking place. Local distribution of time and frequency at lowest uncertainty is realized using bidirectional optical fiber links to customers with Cesium and Rubidium standards.

articleTitle: A compact iodine stabilized external-cavity diode laser at 633 nm with a novel transmission grating
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A portable (32 cm/spl times/13 cm/spl times/6 cm) laser frequency standard has been constructed by frequency stabilizing an external-cavity diode laser to the Doppler free absorption of iodine. The compact structure is achieved by using a novel transmission grating to construct a highly compact external-cavity laser with excellent passive frequency stability.

articleTitle: High-resolution laser spectroscopy of atomic silver
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We describe a measurement of the frequency of the transition 4d/sup 10/ 6p /sup 2/P/sub 3/2//spl rarr/4d/sup 9/ 5s/sup 2/ /sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ near 547.7 nm in neutral silver using laser spectroscopy of a collimated metastable atomic beam and frequency calibration with respect to iodine resonance lines, using laser heterodyne spectroscopy.

articleTitle: The OFMET watt balance: progress report
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new type of moving-coil Watt balance with a compact design is under construction at the Swiss Federal Office of Metrology (OFMET). Several key components of the system have been independently characterized. In this paper, the assessment of the magnet, the optical system for speed measurement and regulation, and the programmable Josephson voltage standard are reported.

articleTitle: A standard calibration system for geomagnetometers
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A precise system (standard) for reproducing a DC magnetic field of the extended geomagnetic range (10-110 /spl mu/T) is established. The uncertainty of the total magnetic field reproduction in SI units is 3/spl times/10/sup -7/ inside a sphere 10 cm in diameter with an rms deviation of 0.002 nT. The uncertainty of the magnetic field direction is 1 second of arc.

articleTitle: Evaluation of ac-dc difference of thermal converters using an SFQ-based D/A converter
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Digital to analog converters based on the Josephson effect are promising for voltage standards, because they produce voltage steps with ultimate precision and stability. We are currently developing an SFQ-Based D/A converter (RSFQ-DA), designed for synthesizing a sinusoidal waveform for metrological applications. In this report, we examine a feasibility of an ac-dc transfer difference measurement for a thermal converter using the RSFQ-DA.

articleTitle: Development of a new levitated-mass mechanism toward replacing the kilogram
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new superconducting levitated-mass mechanism is now being developed with the final target of replacing the kilogram in terms of the fundamental constants. Improving the stability of trajectory by means of introducing a superconducting linear bearing is the issue in question for this development. The strategy of the development, experimental results and further prospects are discussed.

articleTitle: Progress towards a measurement of the bound electron to proton g-factor ratio at 0.6 tesla
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We describe an experiment to measure the ratio of the bound electron to proton g-factor in atomic hydrogen. This is performed in in a magnetic flux density of 0.6 tesla. The electron and proton spin flip frequencies are determined by a least squares fit of the theoretical form of the modulated hydrogen electron spin resonance signal to the data.

articleTitle: Power dependence characteristics of metal foil type standard resistors
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper reports the results of an investigation on the power dependence characteristics of the metal foil type standard resistors. The power coefficient and heating time constant were measured for 10 /spl Omega/, 100 /spl Omega/ and 1 k/spl Omega/ metal foil type standard resistors.

articleTitle: Frequency dependence of the AC quantum Hall effect; comparison of data from two laboratories
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Data is presented showing the frequency and field dependence of the AC quantum Hall effect. In common with previous studies, a marked dependence of R/sub H/ is seen as a function of both frequency and field.

articleTitle: Cryogenic current comparator implementation at CENAM
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The implementation of a Sullivan type [1974], cryogenic current comparator bridge (CCC) is presented. Some design aspects are discussed, such as the need to match the time constants of the current source filters and the modifications in the CCC connections in order to increase the leakage resistance. Some preliminary results are given.

articleTitle: A phase-locked frequency divide-by-three optical parametric oscillator based on periodically poled lithium niobate
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report on the operation of a 3/spl omega//spl rarr/2/spl omega/+/spl omega/ subharmonic doubly resonant optical parametric oscillator (DRO) as an accurate 3:1 phase-locked optical divider of the frequency of a diode laser at 355 THz (843 nm). A fractional frequency stability of 2/spl times/10/sup -17/ of the division process has been achieved for 100 s integration time.

articleTitle: Miniature DC SQUID devices for the detection of single atomic spin-flips: scaling of flux sensitivity with device dimension
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report progress towards a SQUID based system capable of detecting single atomic spin-flips. The scaling of the flux sensitivity with SQUID loop dimension of miniature niobium DC SQUID devices is examined and shown experimentally to vary as predicted. Our smallest device, with loop size 3 /spl mu/m/spl times/3 /spl mu/m, is capable of detecting a few spins in a 1 Hz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Ion beam measurement with a HTS SQUID current comparator
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Superconducting direct current comparators are well established with low temperature superconductors and SQUIDs. We have begun investigations into HTS current comparator designs, with a readout SQUID also made from HTS. This work aims to produce a system capable of high accuracy noninvasive measurement of an ion beam current (in the range 1 /spl mu/A to 1 mA). Measurements of the current ratio accuracy are reported and preliminary experimental results on the measurement of ion beams are described.

articleTitle: Development of Josephson voltage calibrator
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The results of our work towards developing a Josephson voltage calibrator based on high-temperature Josephson junctions array are discussed. The concept of the voltage calibrator and technological aspects of its fabrication are described.

articleTitle: Pulse-handling capabilities of intersecting-waveguide type optical modulators/switches with curved electrodes
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The operation-speed of intersecting waveguide type optical modulators/switches is shown to depend, besides the commonly known device-capacitance, on the propagation-time difference of the guided mode spatial plane-wave components. Further, in fast pulse operations, the modulating information signals applied to the electrode must be properly synchronized to the optical ones.

articleTitle: A thermal power comparator based on the push-pull techniques
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: In this paper a thermal power comparator based on the push-pull techniques of sum-and-difference circuit is proposed. The power measurement by mean of push-pull techniques can reduce an error of unidentical thermal converters, and an error for the deviation from the parabola characteristics of heaters in thermal converters. It is shown that the uncertainty of the comparator can be obtained better than 30 ppm in the input frequency range from 40 Hz up to 1 kHz.

articleTitle: Non-linear spectroscopy of isotopic acetylene at /spl lambda/=1.5 /spl mu/m for absolute frequency stabilization of diode-pumped Er-Yb:glass laser
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Non-linear spectroscopy of the acetylene molecule has been performed in the wavelength range from 1536 nm to 1550 nm, by means of a novel diode-pumped Er-Yb:glass laser with single frequency emission. In order to saturate the acetylene lines, the gas sample was placed within an external high finesse resonator.

articleTitle: An efficient broadband method for equivalent source reflection coefficient measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A method is described to determine the complex equivalent reflection coefficient of RF sources using a mismatched power meter connected to a set of different phase shifting two-ports. The method is efficient, as only simple instrumentation is necessary, moreover, it is a broadband method, applicable to all types of sources and directly traceable to impedance standards.

articleTitle: Analysis of the performances of a digitizer for peak measurement of lightning pulse
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The performances of a digital multimeter used as a digitizer are analysed with the aim of using it as a digitizer in measuring the peak voltage of a lightning pulse with high accuracy. The equivalent transfer function of the multimeter was measured and compared with declared specifications of the multimeter itself. The comparison between the measures obtained by the digitizer and by an alternative method is presented.

articleTitle: An improved CCC and QHR system for resistance standards metrology
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have improved on the design of the integrated cryogenic current comparator (CCC) and QHR system used for the characterisation of standard resistors to the quantum Hall standard of resistance. Improved current sources are used with a larger and more sensitive CCC. The CCC is mounted in a separate cryostat so that both the CCC and QHR system can be used independently.

articleTitle: Optical frequency interval divider based on optical parametric oscillators
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have used an optical frequency interval division method that is based on optical parametric oscillators (OPOs) only to reduce a large frequency difference between 1064 nm of the YAG laser and divided by 3 of 532 nm. The 47 THz frequency span can be measure by the comb of optical frequencies emitted by a mode-locked laser or by the parallel connection of OPOs and optical frequency comb generators.

articleTitle: Current AC-DC transfer measurements in the microampere range
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Two methods for accurate measurement of AC-current in the /spl mu/A-range using a thermal transfer standard with amplified mV-ranges together with current shunts are described. The results of measurements and predictions using the two methods are compared and found to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Nondestructive evaluation of aged 1Cr-1Mo-0.25V steel using first harmonics
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We present a new procedure to evaluate the first harmonics in a 1Cr-1Mo-0.25V steel. The method is based on the existence of the first harmonics in the differential magnetization around the coercive force. The apparatus is based on the detection of the voltage induced in a coil using a lock-in amplifier tuned to a frequency close to the exciting one. Results obtained for the first harmonics and Vickers hardness on the annealed samples, show the peak width of the first harmonics and Vickers hardness decreased as aging time increased. The correlation between Vickers hardness and the peak width of the first harmonics could be evaluated nondestructively.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Josephson voltage standards of VNIIM and PTB
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Comparisons of the 1 V Josephson array voltage standard (JAVS) of the "D.I. Mendeleyev Institute for Metrology" (VNIIM), Russia, with that of the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB), Germany, were carried out in St. Petersburg in June 1999. The results of the direct comparison agree within an overall standard uncertainty of less than 1 nV. The results also show that direct comparisons are useful for detecting voltage offsets of a few parts in 10/sup 10/.

articleTitle: Progress in the development of a high-temperature superconducting CCC
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We propose to fabricate a toroidal cryogenic current comparator from high-temperature superconducting (HTS) materials. The symmetry of our intended design allows high accuracy to be achieved even in the presence of discontinuous shielding. Initial efforts in the fabrication of YBCO (YBa/sub 2/Cu/sub 3/O/sub 7/) components are promising.

articleTitle: The measurement of Newton's gravitational constant with the MSL torsion balance
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We describe the current status of our determination of the Newtonian gravitational constant (G). Since our 1998 determination of G we have been making a measurement of G with our torsion balance operating in a dynamic mode. This paper briefly reports on the uncertainty analysis of our most recent compensated measurement and on our experiences of measuring G with the dynamic method.

articleTitle: A sampling wattmeter with a capacitive shunt for the measurement of power under highly distorted waveforms
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new wattmeter is presented for the measurement of power when the voltage and current are distorted. It uses non simultaneous sampling of the voltage on the load and on a capacitive shunt. As current has usually a higher distortion than voltage, this approach is less demanding for the analog to digital converters.

articleTitle: Reference data on multicharged ions: application to high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The main field of investigations for multicharged ions Spectra Data Center (MISDC) at VNIIFTRI is presented. The detailed description of the database "SPECTR" is considered.

articleTitle: A power-frequency current-comparator-based direct-reading four-terminal resistance bridge
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A current-comparator technique is applied to four terminal resistance measurements for obtaining a highly accurate direct-reading AC resistance bridge at power frequencies. Active circuits are used to establish equal voltage drops between the potential terminals of the two resistances being compared. The bridge features direct reading with six-digit resolution in either per-unit resistance or conductance. Nominal ratios of 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, and 100 are available. A cascading technique using two two-stage current transformers provides extension of the ratio range to 10000000 with a maximum applied current to 10000 A. The ratio uncertainties of the current comparator at power frequencies, including the range extenders, are less than 5/spl times/10/sup -6/ in both magnitude and phase. The bridge is suitable for measuring resistances from 10 /spl mu//spl Omega/ to 10 k/spl Omega/.

articleTitle: Measurement of low impedances with digital techniques for current and voltage compensation
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The introduced measuring system determines low impedances by comparing the current and voltage values of two impedances. The voltages are measured by digital voltage compensators. The currents are determined by compensating the magnetic field of two currents in a magnetic coil. Digital signal synthesis is used for the coherent sources.

articleTitle: A sealed NML 1 ohm resistor
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Six NML 1 ohm resistors have been mounted in sealed cans. The sealed construction will slow the response of the resistor to temperature variations in the surrounding fluid. It also eliminates the chemical effects of the fluid on the resistor. Possible disadvantages of sealing the resistors are being investigated.

articleTitle: Quantum Hall sample characterization
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper describes the initial results of a characterisation study of QHE samples performed at the NMi Van Swinden Laboratorium at the end of 1996. In this work, four different GaAs-based QHE samples were studied at different currents and temperatures.

articleTitle: Improvement of the 10 volt Josephson array voltage standard at the BEV by semiautomated computer control
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A program for the measurement procedure was developed which calculates the voltage of the Josephson Array Voltage Standard with the actual readings of the microwave frequency. The results on low noise measurements with standard cells show, that different conditions of the microwave frequency are taken into account by the program.

articleTitle: A new scanning X-ray interferometer [for basic physical constants determination]
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The need has arisen for a reduction of the present uncertainty of 3/spl times/10/sup -8/ in the measurement of the (220) lattice spacing, d/sub 220/, of silicon monocrystals. This article describes our step-by-step approach towards this goal.

articleTitle: A continuous slow atomic beam for a cesium frequency standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A continuous slow cesium atomic beam was produced from a thermal atomic beam by using a laser-cooling technique. This beam will be used as an atomic source of a frequency standard. The mean longitudinal velocity and the rms velocity width of the slow atoms were approximately 24 m/s and 0.9 m/s, respectively.

articleTitle: Density measurements of silicon crystals by hydrostatic weighing
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: For a determination of the Avogadro constant by the X-ray crystal density (XRCD) method, a primary density standard based was established at NRLM. Based on this standard, a hydrostatic weighing system for comparing the density of solid materials was developed, where the density is determined with a relative combined standard uncertainty of 1.7/spl times/10/sup -7/.

articleTitle: Establishment of 10-V Josephson array voltage standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The use of 10-V Josephson voltage standard based on 10-V array enables us more convenient and reliable 10-V calibration compared to 10:1 divider system at KRISS. Consistency between the two systems was successfully tested with using a 10-V Zener voltage standard. The uncertainty of the new 10-V Josephson array system was estimated to be less than 0.01/spl times/10/sup -6/(k=2).

articleTitle: Simulation of convective currents in density measurements of silicon spherical standards [for Avogadro constant redetermination]
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Within the project on the redetermination of the Avogadro constant through the X-ray-density method, it is necessary to measure the mass of 1 kg silicon spheres with an uncertainty well below 1/spl middot/10/sup -7/. Among the many sources of uncertainty, we investigated the effect of the convective currents caused by temperature gradients inside the weighing chamber.

articleTitle: Characterisation of YBCO/Au/YBCO resistors for HTS Josephson noise thermometry
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A crucial component of a resistive SQUID noise thermometer is the shunt resistor, which is required to have a value <0.1 m/spl Omega/. The problems of contact resistance between normal metal and HTS superconducting thin films have up to now hindered the implementation of an HTS resistive SQUID. Suitable Au/YBCO/Au shunt resistors /spl sim/20 /spl mu//spl Omega/ have recently been achieved and their characteristics under cryogenic operating conditions have been measured using the Josephson frequency-voltage relationship.

articleTitle: Least-squares fitting of the current drift for a DVM-based comparison method
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A method to compensate the variations in the current source using least-squares fitting and its application to the DVM-based comparison method is described. The algorithm allows for nonlinear variations in the current source, and makes it possible to perform measurement series with no need of constant time intervals between them.

articleTitle: The molar volume of silicon: sometimes materials are not what we would like them to be
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: PTB, IRMM, IMGC, NRLM and CSIRO have been cooperating on improving our knowledge of the Avogadro constant N/sub A/ and therefore of the molar volume of silicon. This is done by performing measurements of the interatomic distance a/sub 0/ (in metre) of the Si atoms in a near-perfect Si single crystal, of the density /spl rho/ (in kg/m/sup 3/) of such a crystal and of the molar mass M (in kg/mol) of the Si in the crystal. This paper proposes that, rather than assume perfection of the artefacts (i.e. the single crystals which could include some with voids) and cast doubt on the reliability of the measurement procedures for a/sub 0/, /spl rho/ and M (as a result of observed deviations), it seems to be the other way round: the measurement procedures seem to be more reliable at the stated (small) uncertainty than the variations observed for the molar volume. The measurement procedures with their small uncertainties, enabled to uncover real differences in the crystals.

articleTitle: Progress towards measuring the standard quantum limit using a monolithic sapphire transducer
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The operation of a novel monolithic sapphire transducer (MST) that has low mechanical and electrical losses is presented. The MST senses the motion of internal acoustic resonances through the interaction between electric and acoustic fields. Progress towards measuring the standard quantum limit by implementing a cryogenic MST is described.

articleTitle: Resistance standards with calculable frequency characteristic for calibration of autobalance RLC bridges
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper is a survey and evaluation of principles, features and realizations of resistor standards with calculable frequency characteristic for calibration of autobalance RLC bridges. The standards have coaxial construction where the internal conductor is a metal film resistor. Construction is of a four terminal pair type. The features of the standards are discussed and the practical realization is described.

articleTitle: Measurement of linewidth variation within one external cavity mode of a grating-cavity laser
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have investigated the dependence of the linewidth of a grating-cavity laser on the fine-tuning of the grating dispersion curve relative to the external cavity modes. Variations on the order of 100 kHz were observed experimentally when tuning the laser frequency within one external cavity mode.

articleTitle: Tunable frequency-locked diode lasers
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A heterodyne frequency-locking circuit is being developed to control the frequency of diode lasers. By employing this technique, we can tunably offset-lock the slave laser frequency to the master laser without optical power loss. The frequency tuning range of the slave laser is designed to be 1.1 GHz and the residual beat frequency fluctuation is aimed to be less than 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Response linearity test of biased 1337 traps
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The upper power limit whilst maintaining a linear response of silicon trap detectors operated under bias voltage was measured for different wavelengths. Measurement results confirm that a bias voltage of 10 V extends the linearity limit by factor of more than 10 for very narrow beams and more than 30 for wide beams.

articleTitle: Simulation of electromagnetic wave interaction with long-period fiber Bragg gratings by using of non-traditional method of theoretical investigation
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The proposed non-traditional method of theoretical investigation is free from the above-mentioned drawbacks. It is based on the fact, that a solution of the wave equation in a modulated media is searched in the form of a single expression, but not in the form of generally accepted counter-propagating waves.

articleTitle: Density comparison measurement of silicon by pressure of flotation method [for Avogadro constant determination]
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have developed a new density comparison measurement system to study defect and impurity effects on silicon single crystals, and carried out density comparison measurement for S2-S3 and S4-S5 silicon spheres. Further prospects are also discussed.

articleTitle: IEN calibration laboratory for high precision multifunction instruments
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The aim of this work is to describe the facilities developed at IEN Electrical Metrology Department for calibration of programmable high precision multifunction instruments. The facilities structure, the implemented traceability chain and the performed activity are here reported.

articleTitle: 125th anniversary of the Metre Convention; the past, present and future of the convention
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: After a description of the origin and reasons for creation of the Metre Convention, the author proposes that it will have an increasingly important place in international affairs because requirements for measurements traceable to the SI have become a central feature in trade agreements.

articleTitle: Low phase noise temperature-compensated cryogenic whispering gallery mode resonator operated at 63 K in a closed cycle cooler
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Whispering gallery modes in a miniature temperature compensated composite dielectric resonator (at T/spl sim/63 K) can exhibit loaded Q/sub L/ values above 10/sup 7/ at /spl sim/10 GHz, close to the Cs atomic clock frequency. The high Q of the dielectric resonators can be used to produce low phase noise oscillators limited only by the performance of amplifiers and mixers. Effective mechanical vibration isolation is also demonstrated in a Gifford-McMahon cooler.

articleTitle: Spectral methods in investigations of superconducting open resonators
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A method for calculation of the electrodynamic characteristics of superconducting open resonators is proposed and realized. The method is used for the calculation of the spectrum, Q-factor and field distribution of the excited oscillation types in two-mirror superconducting confocal open resonators with cylindrical mirrors made from copper and superconducting materials. Theoretical results are confirmed by experimental investigations carried out in the millimeter-wave band using the automatic complex.

articleTitle: Absolute frequency measurement of the cesium D/sub 2/ line
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We describe a scheme of absolute frequency measurement of the cesium-stabilized diode laser at 852 nm based on the absolute frequency standard of /sup 87/Rb at 780 nm and well stabilized CO/sub 2/ laser at 9.23 /spl mu/m. The frequency of the CO/sub 2/ laser is stabilized to the center of the 4.3-/spl mu/m saturated fluorescence with frequency instability of 5 kHz. Two diode lasers are stabilized to the center of D/sub 2/ saturated absorption line of Cs at 852 nm and to the center of D/sub 2/ line of /sup 87/Rb at 780 nm with accuracy about 30 kHz, respectively. The sum frequency of the 852 nm and 9.23 /spl mu/m radiation is beated against the 780 nm radiation to obtain the absolute frequency of the Cs D/sub 2/ line. The sum-frequency generation and beat frequency experiment will be finished in the near future and reported in the conference.

articleTitle: Cryogenic noise parameter measurements of microwave devices
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A robust measurement technique, the seven-state-method, which is well suited for noise parameter measurements at cryogenic temperatures is presented. The optimum generator admittance Y/sub opt /and the input admittance Y/sub in/ of the device under test are calculable from noise power measurements with a noise source operated at ambient temperature. Therefore the measurement of Y/sub in/ with a network analyser as needed for other techniques is not necessary.

articleTitle: Phase-locking of extended-cavity diode lasers with frequency offset of 9.2 GHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We constructed a laser system for the use in atomic velocity-selection through stimulated Raman transition in a cesium atomic fountain clock. Two extended-cavity diode lasers were phase-locked with frequency offset of 9.2 GHz. The loop bandwidth of phase-locking and phase error variance were about 400 kHz and 7.4/spl times/10/sup -2/ rad/sup 2/, respectively.

articleTitle: On sampling-filtering digitization mechanism for high-speed wide band signals
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper analyzes conversion errors of time sampling realized by sampling-hold or flash ADC, presents basic principles and implementation scheme of sampling-filter data acquisition technique for high-speed wide band signals, proves an important characteristic of Gauss filter and calculates digitization window width of Gauss filter output pulse.

articleTitle: A Bragg silicon lattice comparator [for Avogadro constant determination]
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The basic principle and results of the feasibility study of a Bragg lattice comparator are described. It combines a Bragg lattice comparator, Hart-Hausermann (H-H) model, with an X-ray angle interferometer for the determination of the angular position of diffraction peaks. Comparisons between Si crystal lattices with an relative uncertainty of 1/spl times/10/sup -8/ are expected.

articleTitle: Zerodur 0.5 pF toroidal cross capacitor
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A toroidal cross capacitor of 0.5 pF, comprising two right cylindrical cross capacitors each of 0.25 pF, has been constructed from Zerodur. The capacitor is intended to maintain the capacitance standard at times when the NML calculable cross capacitor is out of service.

articleTitle: International comparison for RF power in the frequency range up to 18 GHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A Euromet international laboratory comparison (Project 393) has been carried out between 15 national standards laboratories. Thermistor mounts were used, equipped with PC7 as well as Type N connectors. The results show good agreement in measuring the calibration coefficient of the DUTs and in measuring their reflection coefficients.

articleTitle: Low power sensor calibration at KRISS
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: For the power sensors to be used at below 1 mW power range has been implemented a new calibration method where thermistor mounts are used for the transfer of the power standard calibrated in a microcalorimeter.

articleTitle: Progress towards absolute frequency measurement of the /sup 127/I/sub 2/-stabilized Nd:YAG laser at 563.2 THz/532 nm
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We propose a new method to measure the absolute frequency of /sup 127/I/sub 2/-stabilized laser at 563.2 THz (532 nm), based on a frequency difference generation (DFG) of two diode lasers operating in the near infrared: a narrow free running spectral linewidth (<50 kHz) /spl alpha/-DFB diode laser (angled-grating distributed feedback) operating at 281 TPIz/1.067 /spl mu/m (DL1) and a diode laser at 192.6 THz/1.556 /spl mu/m (DL2). The resulting 88 THz-frequency radiation issued from a type IT cut AgGaS/sub 2/ crystal is compared to the third harmonic of our 29 THz-CO/sub 2//OsO/sub 4/ optical frequency standard (OFSI). On the other side, the DL2 frequency is doubled in a periodically poled lithium niobate crystal (PPLN) in order to phase lock the laser to the 385 THz rubidium optical frequency standard (OFS2). The ultimate accuracy of this measurement will be limited by the OFS2 accuracy, which is known at present time with a 3/spl times/10/sup -12/ uncertainty. The diode laser DL1 is frequency doubled in a KTP crystal placed in a ring cavity of a finesse of about 100. With 400 mW of 1.064 /spl mu/m fundamental radiation at the input of the cavity, up to 22.5 mW of green light has been recently obtained. This high level of green power, the large frequency tunability of the laser diode (more than 1 THz in the IR range) and its intrinsic spectral purity (50 kHz) open the way to an accurate spectroscopy of the I/sub 2/ molecule in the 531.5-533.5 nm range. Preliminary results on the frequency synthesis chain are presented.

articleTitle: Frequency flicker limitation in dual oscillator phase noise measurement instruments
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Dual oscillator phase noise test sets are based on a PLL. In order to pull the slave oscillator in the dynamic range of the control, a DC voltage must be added. In an automatic test set this voltage comes from a DAC. We demonstrate that the flicker noise of the DAC yields an additional frequency flicker of the instrument that is not detected with the usual calibration procedures. In some circumstances the DAC noise turns out to be the main factor limiting the instrument sensitivity at low Fourier frequencies.

articleTitle: Development of an optical frequency interval divider centred at 709 nm
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The UWA research group is developing a coherent microwave-to-optical frequency chain beginning with a series of frequency interval bisection stages. The first stage requires a transfer oscillator at a wavelength of 709 nm. Two such oscillators have been constructed from broad area laser diodes (BALs) and a beat signal between the two has been generated with a fast linewidth less than 100 kHz.

articleTitle: Characterization of ADCs using an FM signal
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: In this paper a frequency modulated (FM) sinewave with a known amplitude is used as a stimulus for the characterization of an ADC with the histogram method. The experimental implementation of this technique was incorporated in an automated measuring system, the design, performance and results of which are the subject of this paper.

articleTitle: New stable 10-pF gas-dielectric capacitors
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Gas-dielectric capacitors of 10 pF consisting of only two coaxial cylinders made of titania-silica glasses (TiO/sub 2/-SiO/sub 2/) have been developed. These capacitors have particularly low temperature coefficients, dissipation factors and voltage dependence as well as extremely high stability.

articleTitle: A method to reduce the voltage dependence of high voltage thermal converters
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper describes a method used with a transimpedance amplifier and high value resistors to reduce the voltage dependence of high voltage thermal converters. With this method, both standard thermal converter at lower voltage and high voltage thermal converter are compared at their full range at the same time.

articleTitle: Microwave coupling to large series arrays of SNS ramp-type junctions for programmable voltage standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Large series arrays of Josephson junctions in SNS ramp-type configuration have been realized with contact areas below 0.4 /spl mu/m/sup 2/. The arrays showed excellent current-voltage characteristics with small parameter spread. For the application in programmable voltage standards, special microwave circuits have been developed containing up to 40000 junctions.

articleTitle: A study on the measurements of clock difference using 10 kHz and 1 pps signal
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We made a clock comparison system using the 10 kHz and 1 pps signal. A frequency divider is used for generating 10 kHz signal from the clocks. Clock comparison is carried out by using the system from MJD 51160 to MJD 51196. We compared the results using the 10 kHz data with those using 1 second data averaged for 10 seconds. The precision of clock comparison was improved by using the clock comparison system.

articleTitle: Fast method applied to the measurement of microwave power standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An isothermal method was developed in order to reduce the efficiency measurement time of microwave power standards, using microcalorimeters. Results given from 8.2 GHz to 26.5 GHz in two waveguide standards show good agreement between classical and isothermal methods. The measurement time has been reduce by a factor of more than three, while keeping the same uncertainties.

articleTitle: Intercomparison of nonsinusoidal calibration systems at NRC Canada and SP Sweden
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A portable and stable source of ac voltage and current capable of generating sinusoidal and distorted waveforms was used as a means of comparing the nonsinusoidal calibration systems at the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) and the Swedish National Testing and Research Institute (SP). Comparisons of the test results obtained at the two laboratories were valuable in evaluating the performance of the two nonsinusoidal calibration systems especially when used to measure the amplitude and phase of harmonic voltages and currents in the presence of large fundamental components.

articleTitle: DFB fiber lasers as optical wavelength standards in the 1.5 /spl mu/m region
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Single-mode distributed feedback (DFB) fiber lasers have been frequency locked to selected absorption lines in the 1.5 /spl mu/m region. Wavelength modulation and fast frequency corrections were achieved by strain tuning the fiber laser by piezoelectric transducers. A mechanical lead screw achieved coarse wavelength tuning of almost 3 nm.

articleTitle: The European AC QHE project: summary of the OFMET DC measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A large effort has been launched in many European national laboratories to implement the AC quantum Hall resistance as a practical quantum standard for the AC resistance. This effort is coordinated through an European project. The present paper summarizes the DC characterization made at the Swiss Federal Office of Metrology (OFMET) on several batches of samples especially fabricated at the PTB for this project.

articleTitle: An optical frequency chain for absolute frequency measurement of the 445 THz strontium trapped ion frequency standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Preparations are underway for an absolute frequency measurement of the NPL strontium ion trap optical frequency standard relative to a transportable methane-stabilized infrared frequency standard. The chain exploits the high non-linear conversion efficiency obtained with PPLN and improved diode laser local oscillators at intermediate frequencies.

articleTitle: Progress in linking the farad and the R/sub K/ value to the SI units at BNM-LCIE
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A calculable capacitor and a quadrature bridge are used at BNM-LCIE to link capacitance unit and R/sub K/ value to the SI units. Modification of the calculable capacitance movable guard guiding and revaluation of the transfer resistors frequency dependencies have been done to improve the results of these two direct determinations. Preliminary measurements show that R/sub K/=R/sub K-90/(1+6.6 10/sup -8/) (1/spl sigma/=7.10/sup -8/).

articleTitle: Sensor for the measurement of liquid permittivity using one measurement cell
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A permittivity sensor using sensitive capacitive-dependent crystals is described. Presented is the probe sensitivity (dependence of df on permittivity). In addition, the new idea of excitation of the entire sensor with stochastic test signals is described, and the permittivity surface-measuring method is given. The latter includes the influence of test signals on the weighting function uncertainty. The uncertainty of the surface permittivity measurement is less than 0.01% (T=10-30/spl deg/C).

articleTitle: A new multivalue inductance standard based on equivalents with the switched capacitors
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new transportable multivalue inductance standard built on the basis of circuits of electronic equivalents of inductance with switched capacitors, is described. The inductance range of the standard is 1 mH-1000 H, its frequency range is 20 Hz-10 kHz, the uncertainty is 0.02-0.1%.

articleTitle: Development of a programmable bipolar Josephson-array voltage-standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We describe the development of a programmable alternating voltage source based on a non-hysteretic Josephson array. The array is driven by a sinusoidal signal in combination with a digital code. The code causes the array to rapidly switch between states that correspond to its first positive and negative constant-voltage step respectively. If the inverse switching time is made comparable to the RF-drive frequency, the RMS value of the output-voltage can be calculated accurately.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization at /sup 127/I/sub 2/ Doppler-broadened line center near 532 nm using Nd:YVO/sub 4/ intracavity doubled lasers
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Using an EOM crystal and FM spectroscopy method, we have locked the laser frequency to Doppler broadened lines of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ using intracavity laser systems. The laser gain crystal is Nd:YVO/sub 4/, and the intracavity frequency doubling crystal is a KTP plate. It is estimated that the frequency stability of the stabilized laser is in the order of 10/sup -9/.

articleTitle: Iodine-stabilized 1550 nm diode laser for optical fiber communication
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We present our work on the frequency stabilization of a 1550 nm diode laser by locking its second harmonic to the hyperfine transition of the iodine. This scheme provides a general method to stabilize the frequency of laser diodes in the wavelength range from 1500 to 1600 nm.

articleTitle: Bayesian estimates for calibration chain elements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Summary form only given. Considering the recalibration of a measurement device, we generalize within a Bayesian approach earlier expressions for estimates of the interesting quantities to the case of a calibration chain containing an arbitrary number of elements. As before the obtained new expressions take into account the result of a previous calibration of the elements and give a posteriori estimates.

articleTitle: Accurate selective isotropic measuring system for electromagnetic fields in amplitude and phase
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Broadcast towers are shared by numerous communication systems which generate a very complex electromagnetic environment, and have to comply with safety standards based on ICNIRP guidelines. To verify compliance with those limits, it is necessary to define a new selective isotropic and accurate probe.

articleTitle: A dual-balance high-resistance bridge in the range 1 T/spl Omega/ to 100 T/spl Omega/
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The NIST dual-balance guarded active-arm bridge, using a third dc source and a second detector to balance the guard network, is described. Improvements to the NIST guarded active-arm bridge and the design and construction of improved high resistance standards have facilitated the extension of NIST calibration services to the 10 T/spl Omega/ and 100 T/spl Omega/ decades of resistance.

articleTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Presents the front matter and table of contents from the proceedings.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Automatic high precision audio frequency power standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An audio frequency power standard based on digital sampling was developed. By exactly matching the sampling and power frequencies, the standard allows fast analysis of several hundred harmonics of the mains frequency. Temperature dependence in the sampling voltmeters is the major source of uncertainty.
