articleTitle: Traceable calibration of specific absorption rate (SAR) for mobile phone dosimetry
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper describes an NPL project for providing traceability for SAR measurement in mobile phone dosimetry. Electric field implantable probe calibration facilities have been developed for this purpose. Computer simulation has been used to assist in analysing the uncertainty budgets for these calibrations. A new international intercomparison has been proposed for measurement of this parameter.

articleTitle: Making 1 attoamp measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: New equipment has made possible the measurement of currents with one-sigma uncertainty of 1 attoamp (1E-18A), equivalent to 6 electrons per second. This paper discusses the techniques required to produce stable currents at this level, and filtering and data reduction techniques needed to make the measurements.

articleTitle: 200 k/spl Omega/ AC resistance standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A resistance standard, comprising three 200 k/spl Omega/ resistors mounted in a temperature controlled enclosure, has been constructed from commercially available precision metal foil resistors. The resistance standard is intended for use with a multiple frequency R-C bridge and an AC QHR bridge.

articleTitle: Optical heterodyne refractometry in the microwave range to 100 GHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A novel, heterodyne refractometer, consisting of a Fabry-Perot optical interferometer to which pairs of lasers are locked in wavelength, is being further developed to study the anomalous dispersion of a gas, in order to provide an alternative method to well-established absorption-based techniques of determining gas concentration.

articleTitle: High stabilization of DC-current source on the basis of atomic magnetic resonance in helium-4 [for proton gyromagnetic ratio measurement]
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An atomic magnetic resonance based current source has been developed for a new measurement of the proton gyromagnetic ratio in low field. The high-stability current source is realized by the application of more precise magnetic-field-to-frequency converter. We used the method of /sup 4/He metastable spin polarization through optical pumping of Cs atoms, and also a newly designed two-layer solenoid for the purpose. The drift of current is less than 0.1 ppm/h and its random standard deviation is 0.05 ppm.

articleTitle: A new method and a device for high precision true RMS measurements using the Monte-Carlo-method
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The paper describes a novel method for high precision true RMS measurements of arbitrarily shaped signals. The method is based on a special statistical algorithm and allows extremely high sampling rates. According to a PTB calibration, the uncertainties of a laboratory model proved to be less than 0.01% of full scale at signal frequencies between 30 Hz and 70 kHz.

articleTitle: Fused silica dielectric 100 pF capacitor
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new set of stable, fixed capacitors is under construction at NML to replace the existing standards and to permit a build-up from the calculable capacitor at constant applied voltage. Capacitors up to 50 pF are of Invar construction, while those of 100, 200 and 500 pF are combinations of 100 pF capacitors which will be made from fused silica.

articleTitle: International comparison of a pulse calibrator used in high voltage impulse calibration
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Measurements on a pulse generator, which was made and characterised by NML, Australia, have been made at NRC in Canada and PTB in Germany. The calculated and measured peak values agree to /spl plusmn/0.5% and the front times to /spl plusmn/2.5%.

articleTitle: Automated system for measuring AC-DC transfer difference of TVCs
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An automated system for measuring AC-DC transfer differences of TVCs at a frequency of 1 kHz is presented. The mode of this system functioning is based on measuring AC-DC transfer differences according to definition. The system provides measurement of AC-DC transfer differences of TVCs with uncertainty less than 10/sup -6/ at 1 kHz.

articleTitle: Intercomparison between PTB and UkrCSM of the calibration of standard current transformers and standard voltage transformers
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Within the framework of the regional metrology organization COOMET, the PTB started an intercomparison of the calibration of a standard current transformer and a standard voltage transformer under participation of the SMU of Slovakia, GUM of Poland, UkrCSM of Ukraine and VNIIMS of Russia. The comparison between PTB and UkrCSM was carried out at UkrCSM (Kyiv) in September 1999. It is described below and results are presented.

articleTitle: First results of a calculable capacitor at KRISS
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A calculable cross capacitor has been developed at KRISS through technical cooperation with VNIIM. All mechanical features have been completed and the optical parts of the capacitor are being improved. The first results are introduced.

articleTitle: Do we know the wavelength of laser beams?
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This article deals with the effect of diffraction on the spatial periodicity of laser beams and gives particular attention to improvements in the mise en pratique of the definition of the meter. A general formula links the actual beam wavelength, which is not the same wavelength of its plane wave approximation, to the variances of the transverse components of photon impulse. Therefore, assessment of the values of these parameters is an integral part of the determination of the wavelength of radiations of stabilized lasers.

articleTitle: A capacitance standard based on counting electrons
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have built a prototype capacitance standard based on single-electron tunneling (SET) devices and cryogenic vacuum-gap capacitor. We are currently involved in a thorough uncertainty analysis of the prototype, and we are preparing to make a direct comparison with the calculable capacitor at NIST.

articleTitle: Comparison between the SNS and SIS Josephson voltage standards at OFMET
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Recently, a new Josephson voltage standard based on a 1 V programmable chip provided by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) was implemented at the Swiss Federal Office of Metrology (OFMET). A comparison with a conventional Josephson voltage standard showed a voltage difference of 0.5/spl plusmn/0.8 parts in 10/sup 9/. This preliminary result demonstrates the new system is functioning properly and can be used in various types of measurements. In particular, it will be one of the key components of the Watt balance experiment that is presently under construction at OFMET.

articleTitle: Study of single electron transistor for metrological application
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: SET transistor was fabricated in ETL for meteorological application. Gate modulation for a single electron transistor was observed. TLF-type noise was also observed which depend on cooling time.

articleTitle: Temperature control system for inductance standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The construction of the temperature controlled inductor at UME, based on the electronic principle of the PI (proportional-integral) method which gives 1 mK stability at the set point is reported. The aim of this work is to reduce the uncertainty component which mostly originated from the temperature dependence of the inductance standard for primary level measurements. Some experimental results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Using the Allan variance and power spectral density to characterize dc nanovoltmeters
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Stochastic serial correlations in nanovoltmeter data are often ignored and the experimental standard deviation divided by the square root of the number of observations is incorrectly used to describe the scatter. This paper demonstrates the use of power spectra and the Allan variance to characterize the performance of digital and analog DC nanovoltmeters.

articleTitle: An inductive voltage divider for international comparisons
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An inductive voltage divider has been constructed specifically for BIPM Key Comparison CCEM-K7 and for further use by regional metrology organizations. The divider provides output voltages at all one-tenth and one-eleventh steps of the input voltage, and at one hundredth of the input voltage. It is constructed to withstand the rigours of transport.

articleTitle: Automatic measurements of the voltage dependence of range resistors for AC-DC thermal converters
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new automatic system for measurements of the voltage dependence of range resistors for AC-DC thermal converters, has been set up. Using this system, high precision measurements of the difference between the voltage dependence of the impedance and that of the DC resistance are performed. These measurements have shown that this difference does not fully explain the variation of the AC-DC transfer difference.

articleTitle: On the choice of comparison reference values for the purpose of pair-wise comparison of laboratories
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A reference value is sought that provides unbiased estimates of the differences between any pair of laboratories. It is found that in general no single-valued reference value exists that yields an unbiased estimate of the difference for all possible pairs of laboratories. In all cases the best estimate of laboratory difference is evaluated strictly in terms of differences in results. It is concluded that the concept of a comparison reference value is both unnecessary and unsuited to the purpose of pair-wise comparisons of laboratories.

articleTitle: Influence of connecting cables on the measurement uncertainty in calibration of resistance thermometers
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The main objective of the article is to examine effects of various measuring set-ups and hence the contribution to the total uncertainty in calibration of standard platinum resistance thermometers against fixed points.

articleTitle: An electronic device for increasing the accuracy of high-voltage measuring transformers
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new electronic system to assist high-voltage measuring transformers is proposed. This system compensates the voltage drops in the series impedances, which are the main cause of error in this type of transformer. An adjustment procedure is proposed using a power analyzer as the zero detector. The nonlinear behavior of the magnetizing branch has no influence on the results.

articleTitle: DC voltage synthesis using a pulse-quantized Josephson voltage source
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have synthesized and measured DC voltages using a bipolar pulse-quantized Josephson voltage waveform synthesizer. Bias current ranges were determined for 101 equally spaced DC voltage steps between -18.6 and +18.6 mV. The flatness of a step at -7.444 mV was found to vary only 2.6 nV with a type A standard uncertainty of 1.6 nV. The linearity of a nanovoltmeter was investigated by synthesizing 11 different DC voltages.

articleTitle: Behavior of the travelling standards in the international comparisons of DC voltage ratio
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Two international comparisons of DC voltage ratio up to 1000 V have been started. Unexpected difficulties when directly comparing at high voltage the travelling divider with a reference divider were reported and investigated. From the control measurements at the pilot laboratory (IEN), information about the behavior of the travelling standards in the comparisons can be drawn.

articleTitle: New thin-film multijunction thermal converters with negligible low frequency ac-dc transfer differences
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The ac-dc transfer differences of thin-film thermal converters at low frequencies are caused by nonlinearities of the heat transport mechanisms and of the thermal-to-electric conversion. A compensation circuit has been designed which results in converters with ac-dc transfer differences below 0.3/spl middot/10/sup -6/ at 10 Hz. The standard uncertainty of the ac-dc transfer difference measurement was reduced to 0.3/spl middot/10/sup -6/ at 10 Hz.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the energy loss in superconductors used in the superconducting magnetic levitation experiment
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The energy loss in superconductors is examined by using "flux-up" procedure developed in the superconducting magnetic levitation (MAGLEV) experiment at the NRLM. The energy loss is estimated by observing a hysteresis in a coil current-magnetic flux curve. This approach is also applicable to general use for evaluating superconductors.

articleTitle: The SP Josephson potentiometer quantum Hall resistance standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A Josephson potentiometer method has been developed at SP for Quantum Hall Resistance (QHR) measurements. The QHR 12.9 k/spl Omega/ value is used for the determination of the resistance value of a room temperature 10 k/spl Omega/ resistor. The measurements have given excellent agreement with the maintained 1 /spl Omega/ primary group level.

articleTitle: AC characterization of QHE samples through longitudinal impedance measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Different batches of quantum Hall samples are produced by PTB within the European project "AC Quantum Hall". The AC characterization of the samples by IEN is part of the same project. For each device, the parasitic effects are analyzed by measuring the resistive and reactive components of the longitudinal impedance. First results are shown as examples.

articleTitle: Some new results in calibration of three-phase power/energy comparator in NIM
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: For calibration for three-phase power/energy comparator with class degree of 0.01, a standard equipment with the uncertainty better than 0.01% will be essential. In this paper the relevant work in NIM is reported, including composition of the equipment, influence among phases and comprehension of uncertainty.

articleTitle: A multi-frequency 4-terminal-pair AC bridge
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A 4-terminal-pair AC bridge, capable of a relative uncertainty of 2/spl times/10/sup -9/, has been constructed at NIST. The bridge is a multi-ratio bridge (10:1, 2:1 and 1:1) and operates in the range from 100 to 2000 Hz. The design and initial testing of this bridge is described.

articleTitle: A simple DMM-based measuring system for QHE resistance measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have developed a simple, computer controlled DC measuring system for calibration of wire-wound 10 k/spl Omega/ resistors against a QHE structure. The system employs a high-accuracy DMM in both voltage and four-terminal resistance measurement modes. In both cases, resolution down to 10/sup -8/ and combined standard uncertainty at the level of 10/sup -7/ could be achieved. The system proved to be also useful for testing new QHE samples fabricated for quantum resistance metrology.

articleTitle: Calibration of ac current shunts
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Various methods of calibrating ac current shunts have been developed. The applicability of the methods has been assessed over a range of currents up to 1 000 A at 50 Hz and at lower currents at frequencies up to 100 kHz. The values of the shunts range from 100 /spl mu//spl Omega/ to 10 /spl Omega/.

articleTitle: Measurement of reactive power using a 90/spl deg/ reference and a wattmeter
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A reference standard for VARs is described which uses a calibrated wattmeter with applied voltage displaced by 90/spl deg/ from that of the VARmeter under test. Precise quadrature between the two voltages is monitored using a variation of the NML zero power-factor reference described previously. The uncertainty in VAR measurement is significantly better than that achieved by calculating from watts and apparent power.

articleTitle: Stability measurement of NRLM fountain frequency standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Recent results on the stability measurement of Cs atomic fountain frequency standard at NRLM are reported.

articleTitle: Calibration of electrostatic discharge generators and results of an international comparison
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Electrostatic discharge generators are widely used for testing various equipment with any kind of man-machine interface. The calibration of ESD-generators causes a number of problems such as: the target and the cable set which have a frequency dependent transfer characteristic, the measurement system of large bandwidth etc. A procedure is presented that enables the characterisation of the measurement system and a method is described which allows the correction of the data for the transmission characteristics. Results of an international comparison of ESD-generator calibrations are presented.

articleTitle: Correction of the interpolation error of quadro-phase detection in interferometry
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Laser interferometers using quadro-phase detectors for the fringe counting are frequently used for ultra-precise displacement measurements. The accuracy of interferometers in nanometrology is limited mainly by the interpolation error of the detector system. The new method based on applications of curve fitting using nonlinear last square method was developed for correcting the interpolation error of quadro-phase detectors. The results from the experimental data obtained in interferometrical comparator CMI IK-1 are presented.

articleTitle: Expanding the bandwidth of an asymmetric TEM cell for EMC measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An asymmetric TEM cell with absorber loading is analyzed in terms of field uniformity, bandwidth, and characteristic impedance. This cell was modified from a commercial asymmetric TEM cell to improve its electrical characteristics. It is evaluated experimentally before and after the modification to determine its radio frequency characteristics. The modification and measurement results of the cell are given and compared with the original cell.

articleTitle: A novel open-resonator system for precise measurement of permittivity and loss-tangent
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An open-resonator system is constructed for the precision dielectric permittivity and loss-tangent measurement of low-absorbing materials at 60 GHz. In this new inexpensive simple system, only one frequency source is used together with a liquid helium-cooled InSb detector for the full cavity-length variation technique. This new simple open resonator system provides data with high measurement accuracy although it only uses one fixed frequency source.

articleTitle: Accuracy evaluation of a cesium fountain primary frequency standard at NIST
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Since November of 1998, we have performed five frequency uncertainty evaluations on NIST F-1, our laser-cooled cesium fountain. The results from the latest evaluation have a statistical uncertainty of 1.4/spl times/10/sup -15/ and an uncorrected bias of 0.7/spl times/10/sup -15/. The results have been reported to the BIPM for inclusion in TAI, making this clock one of two cesium fountain clocks used as primary standards in the world. We will present an overview of the evaluations and their uncertainties.

articleTitle: Development of a cold cesium continuous fountain frequency standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A laboratory frequency standard based on a continuous fountain of cold cesium atoms is under development. The resonator is assembled and the continuous fountain is now in operation. Measurements of atomic flux and temperature are under way. An analysis of noise in Ramsey resonators shows that, in continuous operation, the atomic noise rather than aliasing effects will remain the limit to the relative frequency instability down to the low 10/sup -14/ range with presently available quartz local oscillators.

articleTitle: Time- and frequency-domain analysis of fluorescence lifetime for temperature sensors
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A quantitative assessment, both in time and in frequency domain, of data processing methods for measurement of the fluorescence lifetime for fiber optic temperature sensors was undertaken. An experimental comparison, using actual signals received from an optical sensing medium, was carried out and the analysis results compared.

articleTitle: Novel cryogenic capacitor for single-electron charging experiments
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A novel design of a cryogenic vacuum capacitor has been developed which is to be used in our future SET charging experiment. Due to its co-axial design it shows better stability than previous parallel-plate designs. In addition it promises to be better adjustable to a decadic capacitance value.

articleTitle: Construction and evaluation of 100 M/spl Omega/ resistance transfer standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The Slovenian Institute of Quality and Metrology (SIQ) has built some high value standard resistors with values up to 1 G/spl Omega/. They were used for calibration of measurement instruments that use an analog integrator technique to measure resistance. The standard resistors were made of commercially available elements and with our design. Due to the very good results on this project the decision was made that a 100 M/spl Omega/ resistance transfer standard was built. SIQ needs this resistance transfer standard to achieve traceability up to 1 G/spl Omega/. Our interest is to build a good low price resistance transfer standard which will be accessible for a great number of metrological institutes. From first contacts with other National Metrological Institutes in Europe it was noticed that there is an interest in such a standard. Therefore we have proposed a new EUROMET project, which is already agreed upon.

articleTitle: Maintenance and dissemination of the magnetic field unit at PTB
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Based on the value of 1 mT as provided as SI unit for a /spl gamma//sub p/ experiment about 20 years ago, the flux density scale as currently maintained at PTB over a range from 20 /spl mu/T to 2 T by different NMR setups, and the measuring methods used to disseminate the unit in the case of DC- and AC-fields are presented.

articleTitle: Preliminary results from the USNO cesium fountain atomic clock
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We discuss a cesium fountain atomic clock that we have built at the U.S. Naval Observatory (USNO). At the time of this writing, all of the subsystems for the device have been built and final assembly is complete. We expect to present initial data from the device soon. We also discuss different strategies for reporting frequency offsets of the fountain from UTC(USNO) and for steering its local oscillator (crystal oscillator or hydrogen maser). Concurrent with this work we are building a rubidium fountain, that may have even better systematics than the cesium fountain.

articleTitle: Automatic setup for inductance measurement at IEN
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A measurement system that compares an unknown inductor to a standard AC resistor, based on the three-voltmeter method, is presented. The main features of the system are: a two-phase generator for energizing the standards, the four-terminal pair definition of both standards with automatic techniques, a switching unit to employ a single voltmeter, optical links for the distribution of frequency references. Measurements at metrological level have been performed at 1 kHz with inductors in the range 10 mH-1 H.

articleTitle: Suppression of spurious phase shifts in an optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Time-domain atom-light interferometers using a series of beam splitting co-propagating or counter-propagating pulses are employed to identify and to reduce spurious systematic phase shifts in an optical frequency standard resulting from minute wave front curvatures or gravitational acceleration.

articleTitle: Some aspects of GPS receiver application
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The problems to use radionavigational GPS receivers for frequency standard characteristics control are discussed. It is shown, that such problems can be solved for some conditions with help of low-cost GPS receiver SVeeSix-CM3. The results of experimental researchers, which confirm this conclusion are presented.

articleTitle: Direct frequency measurement of iodine-stabilised frequency-doubled Nd:YAGlasers at /spl lambda/=532 nm
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have determined the frequency of the a/sub 1/ component of the P(54)32-0 transition of molecular iodine with an estimated relative standard uncertainty below 1/spl middot/10/sup -11/ using a phase-coherent optical frequency chain from the CH/sub 4/ frequency standard to the visible. This allows the realisation of the meter by visible frequencies with an uncertainty reduced by more than one order of magnitude compared to previous measurements (1999).

articleTitle: On the use of conical reflectors in laser displacement interferometry
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A laser interferometer with 90/spl deg/ conical reflectors was tested. Reflectors with a conic section of 90/spl deg/ in the meridional plane are of interest in a number of applications, including laser displacement interferometry, especially for measurements in submicrometre range, laser spectroscopy, and multi-pass optical cells.

articleTitle: A highly stable tunable cryogenic capacitor
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: In order to realize a quantum capacitance standard, a highly stable vacuum-gap cryogenic capacitor based on a coaxial design has been developed. A tuning mechanism allows to adjust the room temperature value of the capacitance to obtain a value of 1 pF at 4.2 K. At low temperature, the difference between the measured and the target value is smaller than 30 ppm. This summary describes the main characteristics of this tunable capacitor.

articleTitle: International comparison GT/RF 86-1: electric field strengths, 27 MHz to 10 GHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper describes an international comparison of electric field strength measurements at frequencies between 27 MHz and 10 GHz. The participating laboratories were NIST; pilot laboratory (USA), NPL (UK), NMi (the Netherlands), IEN (Italy), LCIE (France), ETL (Japan), KRISS (Korea), and TUW (Poland).

articleTitle: Long-term charge offset and glassy dynamics in SET transistors
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report long-term measurements of the charge offset Q/sub 0/ in SET (single-electron tunneling) transistors, made of Al/AlO/sub x//Al tunnel junctions. In one case, we saw a Q/sub 0/ which was constant (within 0.1 e) over a twelve-day period, except for one excursion of short interval. In most cases, we see a transient (since cooldown) relaxation of the rate of wandering of Q/sub 0/ over one to two weeks, which is very reminiscent of the nonequilibrium heat evolution observed in glasses. We propose that this mechanism drives both the initial high level of noise in SET transistors, as well as the high error rate in SET pumps.

articleTitle: Verification of an automatic calibration process in Italian accredited laboratories
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A description of methods for verifying automatic calibration processes, in an electrical calibration laboratory accredited by the Italian Accreditation Service (SIT Cal Lab), is given in this work.

articleTitle: The strontium single ion standard: application to optical frequency measurements of the 385 THz Rb two photon transitions and the 474 THz I/sub 2//He-Ne standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: An optical frequency standard at 445 THz, based on a single trapped Sr/sup +/ ion, has been developed and applied to the measurement of the /sup 87/Rb 5S/sub 1/2/(F/sub g/=2)-5D/sub 5/2/(F/sub e/=4) two-photon transition frequency at 385 THz. In addition, a single ion based calibration system for the 474 THz I/sub 2//He-Ne standard is described.

articleTitle: Effect of a back gate on the AC characteristics of quantum Hall devices
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: When measured with AC at kHz frequencies the quantized Hall resistance (QHR) of a quantum Hall sample is usually found to be current and frequency dependent. We show that these AC characteristics can be modified by applying an AC potential difference between a back gate and the two-dimensional electron gas. The QHR current coefficient varies with the gate voltage and can be made equal to zero by an appropriate voltage setting. In these conditions the QHR frequency dependence is also reduced.

articleTitle: Measurement uncertainties arising from unpowered shipment of DC voltage references
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Continuously powering the internal temperature-controlled oven provides best accuracy with Zener-diode-based DC voltage references. The hysteresis uncertainties arising from loss of power for two Fluke 732Bs are quantified. This establishes that these instruments can be shipped without battery power between national laboratories without adding significant uncertainty to a comparison.

articleTitle: Measurement assurance in traceable time dissemination
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: In disseminating time, National Metrology Institutes have to ensure that time information received by the users is traceable and uncertainties are evaluated. This paper describes two time distribution systems developed at PSB-a synchronised digital clocks-cluster system, and an automated computer time distribution system. Results of evaluation show that the uncertainties of a few tens of millisecond for both are achievable.

articleTitle: Complete characterization of Zener standards at 10 V for measurement assurance program (MAP)
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A complete characterization of Zener standards for temperature, pressure, and humidity is being performed to improve the uncertainty of a MAP that uses 10 V Zeners as travelling standards. The procedure and equipment used for this work are briefly described. We will report results of evaluating our available pool of Zener standards.

articleTitle: Accurate determination of hyperfine constants of upper level of the P(33) 6-3 transition of molecular iodine using a laser diode emitting around 633 nm
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have performed measurements of frequency splittings of the different hyperfine components of the P(33) 6-3 transition of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ by beat frequency measurements using a laser diode emitting around 633 nm. The four principal hyperfine constants of the rovibrational level v"=6, J"=33 of the ground electronic state have been deduced.

articleTitle: Three-wavelength optical frequency standard based on the two-photon transition in rubidium
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: In this paper, we consider an optical frequency standard offering three simultaneous frequencies at 193, 385 and 578 THz, based on a two-photon transition in rubidium and sum-frequency generation in a periodically poled lithium niobate. Also, we give the theoretical evaluation and measurements of systematic effects shifting the frequency of this standard.

articleTitle: Comparison of high frequency AC-DC voltage transfer standards at NRC, VSL, PTB and NIST
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The paper summarizes results of two international comparisons relating AC-DC voltage transfer standards of the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) to the standards of VSL, PTB and NIST. The first comparison was part of the CCE 92-05 Intercomparison of AC-DC Voltage Transfer Standards at HF (1-50 MHz), designated as a key comparison, with results published before NRC participation. The second comparison was carried out using a calorimetric thermal voltage converter of NRC design. Results of comparisons conducted so far show very good agreement between NRC and the three other NMIs in the frequency range from 10 Hz to 100 MHz.

articleTitle: Meeting the challenge to keep electrical measurements consistent globally
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The system for assuring the consistency of electrical measurements is being expanded through key comparisons. The initial process to select key comparisons is consensus by experts. With experience, the process should become more rigorous. Advances in commerce, computing, and analysis as well as market forces may influence future key comparisons.

articleTitle: Application of SET devices in metrology: Overview of results of the European project SETamp (1997-1999)
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This contribution gives an overview of the main results that were obtained in the European project SETamp (Application of single electron devices for the development of a current standard). Within this project substantial progress was made with respect to the theoretical understanding of the relevant single electron effects, the fabrication and characterisation of single electron transport (SET) devices and the development of high-precision measurement techniques. The so-called R-pump and the RF-SET electron counter have been proven to be very promising for the future realisation of a current standard.

articleTitle: Measuring G with a cryogenic torsion pendulum-a progress report
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We describe the nearly completed apparatus for a measurement of G using a torsion pendulum in the "dynamic" (time-of-swing) mode. Features of the experiment include operation at cryogenic temperature (2K), large pendulum oscillation amplitudes, ring-shaped source masses, and a thin plate torsion pendulum.

articleTitle: Optical heterodyne four-wave mixing spectroscopy with subnatural linewidth
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We introduce an optical heterodyne four-wave mixing (HFWM) spectroscopy with subnatural linewidth. In the HFWM spectroscopy strong bichromatic pump and an arbitrarily intense monochromatic probe field are employed. We show that a coherent two-photon emission by the HFWM process could result in subnatural linewidth.

articleTitle: AC QHR loop measurements
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We have measured the AC QHR using connections which define a closed loop of the device. This allows us to obtain and compare values and field dependencies for both Hall, (R/sub H/), and longitudinal, (R/sub xx/), resistances in the same cool-down. Such measurements allow a more rigorous comparison with DC QHR measurements.

articleTitle: Applying humidity model to reduce uncertainty of voltage comparisons using Zener standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Reported results describe the response of Zener-diode-based voltage standards under relative humidity changes, especially for 1.018 V output, approximately using the solution of a first-order differential equation. It is shown that incorporating a time-dependent humidity correction to the model can substantially reduce the residuals, and therefore the uncertainty, of an international comparison.

articleTitle: Two-way satellite time transfer network in Pacific Rim region
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A Two Way Satellite Time Transfer (TWSTT) network in the Pacific rim region is under construction to contribute to the International Atomic Time (TAI). Four major Time and Frequency Institutes in this region have been conducting long term TWSTT experiments. In addition to these institutes, several ones in this region are planning to join this TWSTT network.

articleTitle: Establishment of resistance traceability chain for Croatian resistance standards
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The main task of Primary Electromagnetic Laboratory ETF in Croatia (PEL-ETF) is to ensure a system of international traceability for the basic electromagnetic standards. PEL-ETF laboratory has established an international traceability chain for its primary group resistance standard in the range of 1 m/spl Omega/-10 M/spl Omega/.

articleTitle: A suspended laser interferometer for determining the Newtonian constant of gravitation
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Progress is reported on an experiment to measure the Newtonian constant of gravitation, G, with a suspended Fabry-Perot laser interferometer. With this technique, we measure the deflection of simple pendulums due to the gravitational attraction of tungsten masses. A result for G is expected with an accuracy of roughly 30 ppm.

articleTitle: Microscope compatible coils for generation of the uniform flat rotating magnetic field
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper describes highly effective coils for generating uniform rotating magnetic field with free optical access to a specimen. The coils consist of the two main mutually perpendicular rectangular coils, inserted one into the other. To make the uniform flat field over the coil surfaces, special correcting coils are used.

articleTitle: Stochastic measurement of PWM signals
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Stochastic true RMS instrument has a wide frequency range, since it works with short data, implied by the use of two-bit flash AD converters and a two-bit multiplier-accumulator. Such a simple hardware allows easy multichannel measurement. Both of the above requirements, wide frequency range and necessity of multichannel measurements, are substantial in the case of measurements on PWM drives. It is shown that the stochastic instrument measures PWM voltages, currents, powers and energies, at the fundamental frequency of 50 Hz, with the same accuracy as their sinusoidal counterparts. This accuracy can be extremely high.

articleTitle: High frequency detection technique for ultra-high resolution spectroscopy of I/sub 2/
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Lines without frequency broadening are obtained by an original technique of second harmonic detection in high frequency modulation transfer. We apply this technique to Raman and degenerated Raman interactions.

articleTitle: Calibration of a standard resistance using a standard platinum resistance thermometer
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A calibrated standard resistance (R/sub s/)is indispensable in order to perform reliable temperature measurements with a Standard Platinum Resistance Thermometer (SPRT). Since in many instances the calibration of such R/sub s/ is difficult to achieve, a novel method for such calibration using two SPRTs, a bridge and a bath is proposed.

articleTitle: A new four terminal-pair bridge for impedance measurements at frequencies up to 1 MHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new four terminal-pair bridge has been developed for measuring capacitance and resistance standards at frequencies up to 1 MHz. The bridge is based on high frequency IVDs, to create voltage ratios, which are calibrated using a "permuting capacitors" device. Preliminary measurements of the capacitance and dissipation factor of a 100 pF standard up to 1 MHz are in good agreement with calculated values, from its measured parasitic impedances.

articleTitle: Capacitance and dissipation factor measurements under high voltage at BNM-LCIE
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: This paper presents the recent improvements to the high voltage capacitors measuring methods used at BNM-LCIE and the new possibilities to come in that field. These improvements are related, among others things, to the use of a carefully calibrated current comparator bridge and to the constitution of standard capacitance and dissipation factor ranges.

articleTitle: Traceability of the 10 k/spl Omega/ standard at IEN
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The traditional scaling method used at IEN for the calibration of the 10 k/spl Omega/ standard is compared with more straightforward techniques, one based on the linearity of a DVM and the other on a commercial current comparator bridge. The results of the three methods agree to better than 1/spl middot/10/sup -7/.

articleTitle: Magnetic flux density standard for low magnetic field at KRISS
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The low magnetic field standard system contains a precision solenoid, Cs-He precision magnetometer, and 3-component compensation of the Earth's magnetic field (EMF). The solenoid produces a standard field which is uniform at better than 0.3 ppm within /spl plusmn/2 cm of the center. The EMF is automatically compensated to 0.1 nT. The standard serves the calibration of magnetometers in the range below 1 mT with 1 nT resolution.

articleTitle: Development of Josephson series arrays for a DC quantum voltmeter
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Josephson series arrays with a binary sequence of nonhysteretic junctions have been realized. The arrays of up to 8192 junctions (14 bit) are operated at microwave frequencies of about 70 GHz. Electronics is under development to build up a fully automated DC quantum voltmeter.

articleTitle: Hybrid interferometer for control of three degrees of freedom
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We describe a quadruple Michelson heterodyne interferometer for measuring longitudinal displacement, pitch, and yaw of a target mirror relative to a stationary one. A Fabry-Perot interferometer provides independent control of systematic errors.

articleTitle: Determination of the gravitational constant using a beam balance
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We describe an experiment to measure the Newtonian gravitational constant G. The gravitational forces of large field masses on test masses are measured using a beam balance. A preliminary result with a relative uncertainty of 220/spl times/10/sup -6/ has been published recently. In the meantime various modifications of the experiment have been made.

articleTitle: Tests on the IEN electrometric ac-dc transfer standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Tests on the electrometric ac-dc transfer standard built at IEN have been performed. The instrument proved to work correctly and to have a stability better than 10 parts in 10/sup 6/ in the period of 5 min. Comparisons with thermal converters have shown results compatible with those obtained by the step-up procedure. Other tests, aimed at investigating the long term stability and at analysing possible systematic effects that can contribute to the ac-dc transfer difference, are also presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Single DVM sampling power meter for low frequencies
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new scheme for power measurement at mains frequencies is presented. It consists of a single sampling voltmeter, double signal generator with trigger circuitry, current and voltage transformers, current shunt and time interval counter. Time interval counter is used to reduce jitter which is introduced within sampling voltmeter. Sampling voltmeter is also used to measure the magnitude of voltage and current.

articleTitle: Interference of atomic states in external field and Lamb shift measurement in hydrogen-like helium
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The principles for observation of the stationary interference pattern of 2sand 2p-states in a uniform electric field are formulated. The optimal values of experimental parameters are estimated.

articleTitle: Evaluation of uncertainty due to excess heating by an adiabatic line in calorimetric measurement of RF power
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We are developing two broadband RF power standards. One is based on 7 mm coaxial line with APC 7 connector for 10 MHz-18 GHz and the other is based on 2.9 mm coaxial line with K connector for 10 MHz-40 GHz. The power measurement principle is calorimetric isothermal control. In these measurements, the effect of excess heating by the adiabatic line becomes important. In the present work, its evaluation method is presented and experimental results are described.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of an optical high electric field sensor
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The present paper proposes an optical device for measuring low frequency high electric fields using a LiNbO/sub 3/ crystal as sensing medium without any contacting electrode. Simulations have been performed in order to find the best design of the sensing element in the sensor.

articleTitle: Development and uncertainty estimation of bridges for the link between capacitance and the QHR at 1 kHz
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Capacitance standard derived from the QHR has been established at ETL. The chain of measurements makes it possible to link capacitance to the QHR at 1 kHz by using the multi-frequency quadrature bridge. The measurement uncertainties in the chain, which comprises resistance bridge, quadrature bridge and capacitance bridge are estimated.

articleTitle: A measurement of the Newtonian constant of gravitation, G, using the BIPM torsion strip balance
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new measurement of G is presented having an uncertainty close to 1 part in 10/sup 4/. It results from work at the BIPM using a novel torsion balance and its aim is to help resolve the discrepancy produced by the 1995 result from the PTB that differed by 0.6% from the then Codata value.

articleTitle: Quick comparison of QHR systems using a 100 ohm transfer resistor
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A resistance comparison carried out with a temperature and pressure stabilized 100 /spl Omega/ standard resistor was performed in November and December 1998. The participants were BIPM, BNM-LCIE (France), PTB (Germany) and VTT (Finland)-pilot. The comparison results agree within 4/spl middot/10/sup -9/ with a combined standard uncertainty of 11/spl middot/10/sup -9/.

articleTitle: Intercomparison of magnetic flux density by means of field coil transfer standard
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The coil constant k/sub 0/-i.e. the quotient of magnetic flux density in the coil centre over the coil current-of a Garrett type field coil has been determined in units as maintained by various standard laboratories. Most of the laboratories have also measured the coil constant k(f) as function of frequency up to f=15 kHz.

articleTitle: Superconducting transition-edge bolometer arrays for ultra-low power radiometry
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: A new generation of ultra-low power bolometer arrays is under development for low background infrared astronomy. This paper describes radiometric measurements on such bolometers using a cryogenic blackbody source with accurately calculable throughput. Because of the very long wavelengths used, roughly 100 /spl mu/m-1 /spl mu/m, the absorbed radiant power differs substantially from that in a classical radiometry measurement, where it would be given by the geometric throughput with small "diffraction corrections".

articleTitle: Imaging of Si-crystal lattice by phase-contrast X-ray microscopy [for Avogadro constant determination]
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: X-ray Moire topography has been improved by the application of phase modulation, imaging, and computing to provide images of lattice distortion with unprecedented sensitivity inside near-perfect Si monocrystals. The technique here presented is based on differential phase modulation to permit the detection of the spatially varying phase shift at the output of an X-ray interferometer of the triple Laue type by the use of a multi-element detector. Information was obtained about the degree of perfection of the crystals being used in the determination of the Avogadro constant and about the effects of machining and etching on the performances of X-ray interferometers.

articleTitle: In-situ calibration of high voltage three-phase transformer loss measuring systems
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The application of a computer-controlled current-comparator-based load loss standard to the in-situ calibration of two different types of high voltage three-phase transformer loss measuring systems at SMIT Transformers is described. The load loss standard simulates a high voltage inductive load at power frequencies which can provide load currents up to 2000 A at any power factor with a resolution of 1/spl times/10/sup -6/, and at test voltages up to 200 kV. It basically provides a known and stable power loss or reference power, determined by the test voltage and the power factor setting, to the transformer loss measuring system, such that its accuracy can be characterized over different voltage, current, and power factor ranges.

articleTitle: Absolute measurement of the Newtonian gravitational constant G
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We present the status and preliminary results for the Wuppertal gravitational experiment which is based on a microwave resonator. The gravitational force of two test masses acting on the resonator is measured as a function of distance. After substantial work in the last half year, we are now again taking data since December 1999.

articleTitle: Influence of frequency difference between current and voltage on ac power measurement result
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: The object of this paper is to draw attention to the influence of possible frequency difference between current and voltage on ac power measurement. We will discuss this issue for wattmeters based on analog and digital sampling techniques in this paper and recommend a optimum sampling interval to be used for the digital sampling techniques.

articleTitle: Recent evaluation results of the atomic fountain frequency standard at PTB
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: We report design features and results of a first uncertainty evaluation of an atomic fountain frequency standard at PTB. The frequency instability contributions of different noise sources are also discussed.

articleTitle: The "Avogadro" problem: summary of tests with null results
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Experiments for the re-definition of the unit of mass by the X-ray crystal density method appear extremely difficult and time-consuming, and no laboratory has reached uncertainties below one part in 10/sup 7/. At present, success is additionally hampered by an unexpected imperfection of the Japanese N/sub A/ crystal, which has not yet totally identified and which causes a spread of the measured data over a range of more than 3 parts in 10/sup 6/ thus pointing to a density lower than that expected by all those involved. Recent progress in the development of moving coil watt balances, a competitive experiment, is, however, motivating: the measurement facilities for N/sub A/ are currently improved and at the same time any density influences on the molar volume are being investigated and proved.

articleTitle: Interlaboratory comparison of Josephson Voltage Standards (JVS) between NIST and Lockheed Martin Astronautics (LMA)
publicationTitle: Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements. Conference Digest. CPEM 2000 (Cat. No.00CH37031)
abstract: Two JVS systems operated at NIST and LMA were compared by using four travelling Zener standards. A MBP protocol was adopted for the comparison. The mean difference between the measurements of the two laboratories was found to be 0.059 /spl mu/V with an expanded uncertainty of /spl plusmn/0.218 /spl mu/V with 95% confidence.
